28:88: God Almighty argues with the polytheists by their recognition of His Oneness and Lordship over the Oneness of His Divinity, so He Almighty says: “Say: Who provides for you from the sky and the earth?” That is, who is it that sends down rainwater from the sky and splits the earth by His power and will, and brings forth from it grain, grapes, herbage, olives, palm trees, gardens thick with trees, fruits, and pastures. Is there a god with God? Then God will say: Is it he who provides for you if He were to withhold His provision? And His statement: Is he who has control over hearing and sight? That is, who gave you this power of hearing and the power of sight, and if He had willed, He could have taken them away and taken them away from you, as God Almighty says: “Say: He is the One who created you and made for you hearing and sight.” And he said: “Say, Have you considered: if God takes away your hearing and your sight” (al-Baqarah 2:17) and His saying: And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living (al-Baqarah 2:17) meaning by His great power and His comprehensive bounty. The disagreement over that has been mentioned before and that the verse is general for all of that. And His saying: And who directs the affair (al-Baqarah 2:17) meaning who has the kingdom of everything in His hand and He protects and is not protected from, and He is the disposing ruler whose rule cannot be overturned, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they are questioned. “He is asked by whoever is in the heavens and the earth. Every day He is in a matter” (al-Baqarah 2:17) so the entire kingdom, the upper and the lower, and what is in them of angels, humans, and jinn are poor before Him, His slaves, and submissive to Him. They will say, ‘God’ (al-Baqarah 2:17) meaning while they know that and acknowledge it. "Say: 'Will you not then fear God'" meaning, will you not fear Him, lest you worship other than Him with your opinions and ignorance? And His statement: That is God, your Lord, the Truth the verse means that this one whom you acknowledged as the Doer of all of that is your Lord and your true God who deserves to be singled out for worship. What is there after the truth except error? meaning, every worshipped other than Him is false; there is no god but He, the One, with no partner. Then how are you turned away? meaning, how are you turned away from worshipping Him to worshipping other than Him, while you know that He is the Lord who created everything and is in control of everything? And His statement: Thus has the word of your Lord come into effect upon those who are wicked the verse means, just as these polytheists disbelieved and continued in their polytheism and worship of other than Him with God, even though they acknowledge that He is the Creator who alone is in control of the kingdom, who sent His messengers with His oneness, for this reason the word of God came into effect upon them that they are wretched among the inhabitants of the Fire, as He said: They said, 'Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers.' God Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, to convey the message and recite the Qur’an to the people, and informing him that He will return him to a place of return, which is the Day of Resurrection, and He will ask him about the burdens of prophethood that He entrusted to him. For this reason, God Almighty said: He who enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely return you to a place of return, meaning He enjoined upon you to deliver it to the people. Will surely return you to a place of return, meaning to the Day of Resurrection, and He will ask you about that, as God Almighty said: Then We will surely question those to whom it was sent, and We will surely question the messengers. And God Almighty said: The Day God will assemble the messengers and say, ‘What was your response?’ And He said: And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, He who enjoined the Qur’an upon you will surely bring you back to a place of return. He means, He will bring you back to Paradise and then ask you about the Qur’an. Al-Suddi said it, and Abu Say’d said something similar. Al-Hakam ibn Abaan said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, He will surely bring you back to a place of return, meaning, to the Day of Resurrection. Malik narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He will surely bring you back to a place of return, to death. This is why there are chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both. In some narrations, it says, He will bring you back to life on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said, He will bring you back to life on the Day of Resurrection. This was also narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Abu Qaz’ah, Abu Malik, and Abu Salih. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, “Yes, by God, he has a place of return. God will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection and then admit him to Paradise.” Other narrations have been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Bukhari said in the interpretation of his Sahih: Muhammad ibn Muqatil told us, Ya’la told us, Sufyan al-Asfari told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He will surely return you to a place of return, he said: to Mecca. This is how it was narrated by al-Nasa’i in the interpretation of his Sunan, and by Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Ya’la, who is Ibn Ubayd al-Tanafisi, and this is how it was narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, He will surely return you to a place of return, meaning He will surely return you to Mecca as He expelled you from it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, He will surely return you to a place of return, to your birthplace in Mecca. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar to this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Yahya ibn al-Juraaz, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Atiyyah, and al-Dahhak. And my father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us: Sufyan said: We heard it from Muqatil seventy years ago, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left Mecca and reached Al-Juhfah, he longed for Mecca, so God revealed to him: Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely bring you back to a place of return, to Mecca. This is from the words of Ad-Dahhak, which indicates that this verse was revealed in Medina, even though the entire Surah was revealed in Mecca. And God knows best. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding the words of God: will surely bring you back to a place of return, he said: This is one of the things that Ibn Abbas kept secret. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Na’im al-Qari’ that he said regarding His statement: He will return you to a place of return, he said: To Jerusalem. And this - and God knows best - goes back to the statement of those who interpreted it as the Day of Resurrection, because Jerusalem is the land of gathering and resurrection, and God is the Grantor of success in what is correct. The way to reconcile these statements is that Ibn Abbas interpreted it at one time as his return to Mecca, which is the conquest which, according to Ibn Abbas, is a sign of the approaching death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas also interpreted Surah When the help of God and the conquest come to the end of the Surah, as the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which was announced to him, and that was in the presence of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Umar agreed with him on that and said: I do not know of it other than what you know. For this reason, Ibn Abbas interpreted at another time his saying: He will return you to a place of return as death, and at another time as the Day of Resurrection which is after death, and at another time as Paradise which is his reward and destiny for carrying out God’s message and conveying it to the two kinds of beings: mankind and jinn, and because he is the most perfect of God’s creation, the most eloquent of God’s creation, and the most noble of God’s creation in general. And the Almighty said: “Say: My Lord knows best who has brought guidance and who is in clear error.” That is, say to those of your people who opposed you and denied you, O Muhammad, from among the polytheists and those who followed them in their disbelief: Say: My Lord knows best who is guided among you and me. And you will come to know for whom the final outcome will be in the Hereafter, and for whom the final outcome and victory will be in this world and the hereafter. Then the Almighty said, reminding His Prophet of His great blessing upon him and upon the servants when He sent him to them: And you did not expect that the Scripture would be revealed to you, meaning you did not think before the revelation was sent down to you that the revelation would be sent down to you, but it is a mercy from your Lord, meaning that the revelation was sent down to you from God out of His mercy towards you and the servants because of you. So if He grants you this great blessing, then never be a supporter, meaning a helper, of the disbelievers, but separate from them, oppose them, and disagree with them. And let not them turn you away from the verses of God after they have been sent down to you, meaning do not be affected by their opposition to you and their turning people away from your path. Do not turn away from that and do not care about it, for God is the one who will support your word, support your religion, and make manifest what He sent you with over all other religions. For this reason He said: And invite to your Lord, meaning to the worship of your Lord alone, with no partner, and do not be of those who associate others with Him. And His statement: “And do not invoke with God another deity. There is no deity except Him.” That is, worship is not appropriate for anyone except Him, and divinity is not appropriate except for His greatness. And His statement: Everything will perish except His Face is informing us that He is the Everlasting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, to whom creation dies but He does not die, as God the Most High said: Everything on it will perish, but the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain. So He expressed the Face as referring to the Self. And similarly His statement here: Everything will perish except His Face means except Him. It has been proven in the Sahih on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The most truthful statement that the poet Labid said is: ‘Beware, everything other than God is false.’” Mujahid and Ath-Thawri said regarding His statement: Everything will perish except His Face meaning except that by which His Face is intended. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih as confirmed by it. Ibn Jarir said: Those who say that cite as evidence the words of the poet: I ask forgiveness of God for a sin that I cannot count. To Him belongs the face and the action. This statement does not contradict the first statement, as this is a statement that all actions are invalid except for those done for the sake of God Almighty, from righteous deeds that are in accordance with the Shariah. The implication of the first statement is that all beings are perishable and fleeting except for His Essence, the Most High and Most Holy, for He is the First and Last, who is before everything and after everything. Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya said in the Book of Reflection and Consideration: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Umar bin Saleem Al-Bahili told us, Abu Al-Walid told us: When Ibn Umar wanted to examine his heart, he would go to a ruined place, stand at its door and call out in a sad voice, saying, Where are my people? Then he would come back to himself and say, Everything will perish except His Face. His statement, To Him belongs the judgement means the kingdom and control, and there is no question of His judgement. And to Him you will be returned means on the Day of Resurrection, and He will reward you for your deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil. End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Qasas. All praise and thanks are due to God.
28:83: These are the attributes of the believing servants of God, who walk on the earth humbly, that is, with serenity and dignity, without arrogance or haughtiness, as God the Almighty says: And do not walk on the earth exultantly, the verse. As for these people, they walk without arrogance or exultation, nor wickedness or haughtiness. It is not meant that they walk like the sick, with affectation and hypocrisy. When the master of the children of Adam, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, walked, it was as if he was descending from a steep slope, and as if the earth was being folded up for him. Some of the early Muslims disliked walking weakly and affectively, to the point that it was narrated on the authority of Omar that he saw a young man walking slowly, so he said: What is the matter with you? Are you sick? He said: No, Commander of the Faithful. So he hit him with the whip and ordered him to walk with strength. What is meant by gentleness here is calmness and dignity, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you come to prayer, do not come to it running, but come to it with calmness. Pray whatever you catch up with of it, and complete whatever you miss.” Abdullah bin Mubarak said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Mukhtar, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, regarding his statement, And the servants of the Most Merciful, the verse, he said: The believers are a people who have been humbled. By God, their ears, eyes, and limbs have been humbled, so much so that you would think they were sick, but there is no sickness in the people. By God, they are healthy, but fear has entered them as no one else has, and their knowledge of the Hereafter has prevented them from this world. So they said, Praise be to God, who has removed sorrow from us. By God, they were not saddened by what saddens people, nor was anything that they sought Paradise for greater than themselves, but fear of the Fire made them cry. Whoever does not seek comfort from God’s comfort will be cut off from this world with regrets. Whoever does not see God’s blessings except in food or drink, his knowledge has become small and his punishment is imminent. God the Almighty says: "And when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace.'" That is, if the ignorant speak ill of them, they do not respond in kind. Rather, they pardon and overlook, and only say good things, just as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was only made more forbearing by the ignorant person's harshness towards him, and just as God the Almighty says: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it. Imam Ahmad narrated: Aswad ibn Amir told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Abu Khalid Al-Walibi, on the authority of Al-Nu'man ibn Muqrin Al-Muzani, who said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'A man insulted another man in his presence, so the insulted man kept saying, 'Upon you be peace,' to the man. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'There is an angel between you who defends you. Whenever this one insults you, he says to him, 'Rather, you, and you have more right to it.' And if you say to him, 'Upon you be peace,' he says, 'No, rather upon you, and you have more right to it.'" Its chain of transmission is hasan, and they did not include it in their collections. Mujahid said, "They said, 'Peace,'" meaning they said, In the hours before dawn, they would ask forgiveness. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, They responded with a good word. Al-Hasan al-Basri said, "They said, 'Peace,'" meaning they are forbearing and not ignorant if they are ignorant of what they say. They accompany God's servants during the day with what they hear. Then he mentioned that their night is the best night, as God the Almighty said, And those who spend the night prostrating and standing before their Lord, meaning in His obedience and worship, as God the Almighty said, They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness. And His statement, Their sides forsake their beds, the verse. God the Almighty said, Is one who is devout during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? The verse. For this reason, God the Almighty said, "And those who say, 'Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever lasting.'" meaning, it is always present, as the poet said: If he tortures, it is a loss, and if he gives generously, he does not care. That is why Al-Hasan said regarding His statement, Indeed, its punishment is a grievance, that everything that befalls the son of Adam and is removed from him is not a grievance. Rather, a grievance is constant as long as the heavens and the earth endure. Sulayman At-Taymi said the same. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said, Indeed, its punishment is a grievance, meaning the blessings they enjoyed in this world. God asked the disbelievers about the blessings but they did not return them to Him, so He made them suffer and cast them into the Fire. Indeed, it is an evil settlement and a place to stay, meaning, what an evil sight is the home and what an evil resting place is. Ibn Abi Hatim said regarding His statement, Indeed, it is an evil settlement and a place to stay, my father told us, Al-Hasan ibn Ar-Rabi’ told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, from Al-A’mash, from Malik ibn Al-Harith, who said: When a man is thrown into the Fire, he falls into it. When he reaches one of its gates, it is said to him, Stay where you are until you are satiated. He said, Then he is given a cup of the poison of lions and scorpions. He said, The skin is separated, the hair is separated, the nerves are separated, and the veins are separated. He also said: My father told us, Al-Hasan bin Al-Rabi’ told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, who said: In Hell there are pits in which there are snakes the size of camels, and scorpions the size of dark-skinned mules. When they are thrown into Hell, they come out to them from their habitats, and seize their lips, skin, and hair, and scrape their flesh down to their feet. When they feel the heat of Hell, they return. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Salam - meaning Ibn Maskeen - told us, on the authority of Abu Dhilal, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A servant in Hell will call out for a thousand years: ‘O Compassionate, O Generous.’ God Almighty will say to Gabriel: ‘Go and bring this servant of Mine to Me.’ Gabriel will set out and find the people of Hell prostrate and weeping. He will return to his Lord, Almighty and Majestic, and inform Him. God Almighty will say: ‘Bring him to Me, for he is in such and such a place.’ So he will bring him and make him stand before his Lord, Almighty and Majestic, and He will say to him: ‘O My servant, how did you find your place and your resting place?’ He will say: ‘O Lord, the worst place and the worst resting place.’ God Almighty will say: ‘Return My servant.’ He will say: ‘O Lord, I did not hope that when You brought me out of it that You would return me to it.’ God Almighty will say: ‘Leave My servant alone.’” God the Almighty said: {And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly} (al-Baqarah 2:17), meaning they are not wasteful in their spending, spending more than necessary, nor miserly with their families, falling short in their rights and not sufficing them. Rather, they are just and virtuous. The best of matters are those that are in the middle, neither this nor that, and are in between the two positions, as God the Almighty said: {And do not make your hand as tied to your neck nor extend it completely} (al-Baqarah 2:17). Imam Ahmad said: Issam bin Khalid told us, Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Abi Maryam al-Ghassani told me, on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: Part of a man’s understanding is his moderation in his livelihood. They did not include this verse. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Ubaidah al-Haddad told us, Maskeen bin Abdul Aziz al-Abdi told us, Ibrahim al-Hijri told us, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: He who is moderate will not be poor. They did not include this verse. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Ahmad bin Yahya told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Maymun told us, Saeed bin Hakim told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Habib, on the authority of Bilal - meaning Al-Absi - on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: How excellent is moderation in wealth, and how excellent is moderation in poverty, and how excellent is moderation in worship. Then he said: We do not know of it being narrated except from the hadith of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: There is no extravagance in spending in the way of God. Iyas bin Muawiyah said: Whatever you do exceeds the command of God is extravagance. Someone else said: Extravagance is spending in disobedience to God, the Almighty. God the Almighty informs us that the Hereafter and its everlasting bliss that does not change or disappear, He made it for His believing and humble servants who do not desire exaltation on earth, meaning to be haughty and arrogant towards God's creation, or to cause corruption among them, as Ikrimah said: Exaltation means tyranny. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: Exaltation means transgression. Sufyan ibn Saeed al-Thawri said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin: Exaltation on earth means unjust arrogance, and corruption is taking money unjustly. Ibn Jurayj said: They do not desire exaltation on earth out of arrogance and haughtiness nor corruption by committing sins. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ash’ath al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Salam al-A’raj, on the authority of Ali, who said: A man may like the strap of his sandal to be better than the strap of his companion’s sandal, so it is included in the words of God the Almighty: “That is the home of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.” This is understood to mean if he intended thereby to boast and to be arrogant towards others, for that is reprehensible, as it is proven in the Sahih that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: It has been revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one boasts over another and no one transgresses against another. But if he likes that merely for the sake of adornment, then there is nothing wrong with it, as it is proven that a man said: O Messenger of God, I like my cloak and shoes to be nice, so is that arrogance? He said: No, God is beautiful and loves beauty. And God the Almighty said: Whoever brings a good deed meaning on the Day of Resurrection will have better than it meaning God’s reward is better than the servant’s good deed, so how can God multiply it many times over? This is the status of grace. Then He said: And whoever brings an evil deed - those who do evil will not be recompensed except for what they used to do as He said in the other verse: “And whoever brings an evil deed - their faces will be thrown into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?” This is the status of grace and justice.
28:1: Surah Al-Qasas Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Adam told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ma’dikarib, who said: We came to Abdullah and asked him to recite to us Surat Ta-Sin-Matin, and he said: I do not have it with me, but you should go to the one who took it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Khabbab ibn al-Arat. He said: So we came to Khabbab ibn al-Arat, and he recited it to us, may God be pleased with him. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful We have already discussed the separate letters, and His statement: Those meaning these are the verses of the clear Book meaning the clear and evident one that reveals the truth of matters, and the knowledge of what has been and what will be. And His statement: We recite to you, [O Muhammad], from the report of Moses and Pharaoh in truth the verse, just as God Almighty said: We narrate to you the best of stories meaning We mention to you the matter as it was as if you were seeing it and as if you were present. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land meaning he was arrogant, tyrannical and transgressed and made its people sects meaning types, each type being directed to whatever he wanted of the affairs of his state. And the Almighty’s saying: He oppressed a group of them means the Children of Israel, and at that time they were the best people of their time. And this mighty and powerful king was empowered over them, using them in the worst of jobs, and toiling them day and night in his work and the work of his subjects, and in addition to this he killed their sons and took their women captive, as an insult to them and a sign of contempt and fear that the boy would be found among them, which he and the people of his kingdom had feared would be found among them, who would be the cause of his destruction and the loss of his state at his hands. The Copts had received this from the Children of Israel in what they were studying from the words of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he entered the land of Egypt, and what happened to him with its tyrant happened when he took Sarah to take her as a slave, so God protected her from him and prevented him from her with His power and authority, so Abraham, peace be upon him, gave good report to his son that from his loins and offspring would be born someone who would destroy the king of Egypt at his hands, so the Copts were talking about this to Pharaoh, so Pharaoh was cautious of that, and ordered the killing of the males of the Children of Israel, and caution will not benefit from destiny, because when God’s time comes, it is not delayed, and for every time there is a book, and for this reason God Almighty said: “And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them heirs * And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared.” And God Almighty did that to them, as He Almighty said: “And We caused the people who were oppressed to inherit the eastern regions of the land and the western regions which We had blessed, and the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because they patiently endured, and We destroyed what Pharaoh had been making.” And his people and what they were building.” And the Almighty said: Thus We caused it to be an inheritance for the Children of Israel. Pharaoh wanted, by his power and strength, to escape from Moses, but that did not benefit him with the power of the Great King whose decree is not disobeyed or defeated. Rather, his judgment was carried out and his pen wrote in antiquity that Pharaoh’s destruction would be at his hands. Rather, this boy, from whose existence you were cautious and because of whom you killed thousands of children, would be raised and brought up on your bed and in your home, and his food would be from your food while you raised him, pampered him, and sacrificed for him. Your death, your destruction, and the destruction of your soldiers would be at his hands, so that you may know that the Lord of the high heavens is the Subduer, the Victorious, the Great, the Strong, the Mighty, the Severe, the Impossible, Whose wills will be, and what He does not will will not be.

28:7: They mentioned that when Pharaoh killed many of the male children of the Children of Israel, the Copts feared that the Children of Israel would be wiped out, and they would be subjected to the hard work they were doing. So they said to Pharaoh: If this situation continues, their old men will soon die and their boys will be killed. Their women will not be able to do the work their men do, so that will be ours. So he ordered that the children be killed one year and left alone the next. Aaron, peace be upon him, was born in the year in which the children were left alone, and Moses was born in the year in which the children were killed. Pharaoh had people assigned to do this, and midwives who would take care of the women. Whoever they saw had become pregnant, they would count her name. When the time of her birth came, only the Coptic women would accept her. If the woman gave birth to a girl, they would leave her and go, but if she gave birth to a boy, those slaughterers would enter with their sharp blades, kill him, and leave. May God curse them. When Moses’ mother became pregnant with him, no signs of pregnancy appeared on her like others, and the midwives did not notice it. But when she gave birth to a boy, she became fed up with him, and feared for him intensely, and loved him with an excessive love. No one saw Moses, peace be upon him, without loving him. Happy is he who loves him by nature and by law. God Almighty said: And I bestowed upon you love from Me. When she became fed up with him, it was inspired in her secret, and it was cast into her mind, and it was whispered in her heart, as God Almighty said: “And We inspired the mother of Moses, ‘Suckle him, but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him one of the messengers.’” Her house was on the bank of the Nile, so she made a coffin and made a cradle in it, and she began to nurse her son. When someone she feared entered upon her, she would go and put him in that coffin, and send him out into the sea and tie him with a rope beside her. One day, someone she feared entered upon her, so she went So she put him in that chest and sent him into the sea, and she forgot to tie him up, so he went with the water and carried him until he passed by Pharaoh’s house, and the maids picked him up and carried him and went with him to Pharaoh’s wife, not knowing what was in it, and they feared that he would tempt her to open it without her, and when he was uncovered, behold, he was a boy of the best, most beautiful, sweetest and most splendid creation, so God put his love in her heart when she looked at him, and that was for her happiness and what God wanted of her honor and the misery of her husband, and for this reason He said: So Pharaoh’s family picked him up so that he might become for them an enemy and a grief verse. Muhammad bin Ishaq and others said: The lam here is the lam of consequence, not the lam of justification, because they did not mean that by picking him up, and there is no doubt that the apparent meaning of the wording requires what they said, but if we look at the meaning of the context, then the lam remains for justification, because its meaning is that God Almighty destined them to pick him up to make him an enemy and a grief for them, so it would be more effective in nullifying their caution against him, and for this reason God Almighty said: “Indeed, Pharaoh, Haman, and their soldiers were wrongdoers. It was narrated that the Commander of the Faithful, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with him, wrote a letter to a group of Qadarites denouncing them for denying the Book of God and His decrees that are based on His foreknowledge. Moses, in God’s foreknowledge, was an enemy and a source of grief to Pharaoh. God Almighty said: “And We showed Pharaoh, Haman, and their soldiers from them that which they had feared.” And you said, If Pharaoh had willed, Moses would have been a friend and a supporter. God Almighty says: So that he would be to them an enemy and a cause of grief. God the Almighty says: And the wife of Pharaoh said, 'A comfort of the eye for me and for you' (Al-Baqarah 2:17), meaning that when Pharaoh saw him, he intended to kill him for fear that he was one of the Children of Israel. But his wife, Asiya bint Muzahim, began to argue on his behalf, defend him, and endear him to Pharaoh. She said, A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Pharaoh said, As for you, yes, but as for me, no. So it was, and God guided her because of him and destroyed him at his hands. This story was mentioned in full in the Hadith of the trials in Surah Taha, narrated by Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, as reported by An-Nasa'i and others. His statement, Perhaps he will benefit us, and that happened to her, and God guided her because of him and made her dwell in Paradise because of him. His statement, Or we adopt him as a son, means that she wanted to adopt him as a son, because she had no children from him. God the Almighty says, and they perceive not, meaning that they did not know the great and conclusive wisdom and decisive proof that God intended by them to adopt him.

28:10: God the Almighty says, informing us about the heart of Moses' mother when her son went into the sea, that it became empty, that is, of everything in this world except for Moses. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Ubaidah, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah and others. She was about to disclose him means that she was about to disclose, due to the intensity of her grief, sorrow and regret, that her son had gone, and to disclose her condition, had it not been for God's steadfastness and patience. God the Almighty says: "Had We not strengthened her heart so that she would be among the believers. * And she said to his sister, "Follow him meaning that she ordered her daughter, who was an adult and could understand what was being said to her, so she said to her, Follow him" meaning follow his traces, get report of him, and seek out his affairs from the outskirts of the city. So she went out for that purpose. "And she saw him from afar" Ibn Abbas said: from afar. Mujahid said: she saw him from afar. Qatada said: She kept looking at him as if she did not want him. When Moses (peace be upon him) settled in Pharaoh's house and the king's wife loved him and divorced him, they offered him the wet nurses in their house, but he did not accept a breast from them and refused to accept any of them. So they went out with him to the market to see if they could find a woman who would be suitable to breastfeed him. When she saw him in their hands, she recognized him but did not reveal that, and they did not notice her. God the Almighty said: {And We had forbidden him wet nurses before}, meaning a predestined prohibition. That was because of his honor before God and His protection for him to be breastfed by anyone other than his mother. And because God the Almighty made that a reason for his return to his mother to breastfeed him, and she was safe after she had been afraid. 28:14: When God the Almighty mentioned the beginning of the matter of Moses, peace be upon him, he mentioned that when he reached maturity and was well-adjusted, God gave him wisdom and knowledge. Mujahid said: He means prophethood. And thus do We reward the doers of good. Then God the Almighty mentioned the reason for his attainment of what God the Almighty had destined for him of prophethood and speaking in the matter of his killing the Copt who was the reason for his departure from Egypt to the land of Madyan. God the Almighty said: And he entered the city at a time when its people were unaware. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That was between sunset and night prayers. Ibn Al-Munkadir said on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That was midday. Sa’id bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, As-Suddi and Qatadah said the same. And he found therein two men fighting meaning they were fighting and disputing. This one was of his party meaning an Israelite and this one was of his enemy meaning a Copt. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, As-Suddi and Muhammad bin Ishaq. So the Israelite called for help from Moses, peace be upon him, and Moses found an opportunity, which was that the people were not paying attention, so he went to the Copt. And Moses struck him and killed him. Mujahid said: So he struck him means he stabbed him with the palm of his hand. Qatada said: He struck him with a stick that was with him, and he was killed, meaning that it was his death, so he died. Moses said: This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy. He said: My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me. So He forgave him. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful. He said: My Lord, because You have bestowed favor upon me, I will never be a supporter, meaning a helper, for the criminals, meaning those who disbelieve in You and disobey Your command.

So he passed by some roads, and there was the one whom he had sought help from the previous day against that Copt fighting another. When Moses passed by him, he called for his help against the other, and Moses said to him, Indeed, you are clearly a heretic, that is, one who is clearly misguided and full of evil. Then Moses resolved to strike that Copt, but the Israelite, due to his weakness, humiliation, and humiliation, believed that Moses only wanted to target him when he heard him say that. When that Copt heard it, he took it from his mouth, then went with it to Pharaoh's door and threw it down before him. Pharaoh learned of that, and his anger intensified, and he resolved to kill Moses, so they sought him out and sent after him to bring him for that purpose.

28:20: God Almighty said: And there came a man He described him as a man, because he took a different path, so he took a path closer to the path of those who were sent after him, so he preceded Moses and said to him: O Moses, the eminent ones are conspiring against you meaning they are consulting about you to kill you, so leave meaning from the city I am to you among the sincere advisors.
28:21: When that man told him what Pharaoh and his state had conspired to do with him, he left Egypt alone. He had not been used to that before, but had been in luxury, comfort, and leadership. So he went out from it, fearful and watching. That is, looking around. He said, ‘My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.’ That is, from Pharaoh and his people. They mentioned that God Almighty had sent him an angel on a horse, who guided him to the way. God knows best. And when he turned toward Madyan, that is, he took a passable, well-trodden path, he was happy about that. He said, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.’ That is, the most upright path. So God did that with him and guided him to the straight path in this world and the hereafter, making him a guide who was guided. And when he came to the water of Madyan, that is, when he arrived at Madyan and came to its water, and it had a well that the shepherds used to go to, He found there a group of people watering. That is, a group watering. And he found besides them two women holding back. That is, holding back. Their sheep were to be returned with the sheep of those shepherds lest they be harmed. When Moses, peace be upon him, saw them, he felt compassion for them and had mercy on them. He said, What is the matter with you? meaning, what is the matter with you that you do not return with these people? They said, We cannot water our flocks until the shepherds depart. Meaning, we will not be watered until these people have finished. And our father is a very old man. Meaning, this is the situation that compels us to do what you see. God, the Most High, said, So he watered for them. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abdullah told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that when Moses, peace be upon him, came to the well of Madyan, he found a group of people watering their flocks. He said, “When they had finished, they put the rock back on the well, and only ten men could lift it. Then he saw two women holding back their flocks. He said, “What is the matter with you?” They told him, so he went to the rock and lifted it. Then he did not draw water except for one drop until the sheep had had their fill. Sahih chain of transmission. And the Almighty said: Then he turned to the shade and said, ‘My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need.’ Ibn Abbas said: Moses traveled from Egypt to Madyan, having no food except herbs and tree leaves, and he was barefoot. By the time he reached Madyan, the soles of his feet had fallen off, and he sat in the shade, although he was the best of God’s creation, and his stomach was stuck to his back from hunger, and the greenery of the herbs could be seen from inside his stomach, and he was in need of a piece of date. And his saying to the shade, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, and Al-Suddi said: He sat under a tree. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn ibn Amr Al-Anqazi told me, my father told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Mas`ud - who said: I urged my camel on for two nights until I reached Madyan in the morning. I asked about the tree under which Moses had taken refuge. It was a lush green tree. I urged my camel towards it, as it was hungry, so my camel took it and treated it for a while, then spat it out. So I supplicated to God for Moses, peace be upon him, and then I left. And in a narration on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, he went to the tree from which God spoke to Moses, as will come, God willing. And God knows best. Al-Suddi said: The tree was from the samr tree. Ata` ibn Al-Sa`ib said: When Moses said, My Lord, indeed I, for whatever good You may send down to me, am in need, he heard the woman.

So he went out from it, fearful and watching. That is, looking around. He said, ‘My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.’ That is, from Pharaoh and his people. They mentioned that God Almighty had sent him an angel on a horse, who guided him to the way. God knows best. And when he turned toward Madyan, that is, he took a passable, well-trodden path, he was happy about that. He said, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.’ That is, the most upright path. So God did that with him and guided him to the straight path in this world and the hereafter, making him a guide who was guided. And when he came to the water of Madyan, that is, when he arrived at Madyan and came to its water, and it had a well that the shepherds used to go to, He found there a group of people watering. That is, a group watering. And he found besides them two women holding back. That is, holding back. Their sheep were to be returned with the sheep of those shepherds lest they be harmed. When Moses, peace be upon him, saw them, he felt compassion for them and had mercy on them. He said, What is the matter with you? meaning, what is the matter with you that you do not return with these people? They said, We cannot water our flocks until the shepherds depart. Meaning, we will not be watered until these people have finished. And our father is a very old man. Meaning, this is the situation that compels us to do what you see. God, the Most High, said, So he watered for them. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abdullah told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that when Moses, peace be upon him, came to the well of Madyan, he found a group of people watering their flocks. He said, “When they had finished, they put the rock back on the well, and only ten men could lift it. Then he saw two women holding back their flocks. He said, “What is the matter with you?” They told him, so he went to the rock and lifted it. Then he did not draw water except for one drop until the sheep had had their fill. Sahih chain of transmission. And the Almighty said: Then he turned to the shade and said, ‘My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need.’ Ibn Abbas said: Moses traveled from Egypt to Madyan, having no food except herbs and tree leaves, and he was barefoot. By the time he reached Madyan, the soles of his feet had fallen off, and he sat in the shade, although he was the best of God’s creation, and his stomach was stuck to his back from hunger, and the greenery of the herbs could be seen from inside his stomach, and he was in need of a piece of date. And his saying to the shade, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, and Al-Suddi said: He sat under a tree. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn ibn Amr Al-Anqazi told me, my father told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Mas`ud - who said: I urged my camel on for two nights until I reached Madyan in the morning. I asked about the tree under which Moses had taken refuge. It was a lush green tree. I urged my camel towards it, as it was hungry, so my camel took it and treated it for a while, then spat it out. So I supplicated to God for Moses, peace be upon him, and then I left. And in a narration on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, he went to the tree from which God spoke to Moses, as will come, God willing. And God knows best. Al-Suddi said: The tree was from the samr tree. Ata` ibn Al-Sa`ib said: When Moses said, My Lord, indeed I, for whatever good You may send down to me, am in need, he heard the woman.
