28:25: When the two women quickly returned with the sheep to their father, he was dismayed by their quick arrival. He asked them about their situation, and they told him what Moses had done. He sent one of them to invite him to her father. God the Almighty said: Then one of them came to him walking shyly, meaning the gait of a free woman, as narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Omar may God be pleased with him, who said: She was hiding behind the sleeve of her armor. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Nu'aym told us, Isra'il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: Omar may God be pleased with him said: She came walking shyly, holding her garment over her face, not a slutty woman, neither a coquettish nor a slut. This is a sound chain of transmission. Al-Jawhari said: The salafi' is a bold man, a strong-willed woman, and a strong camel. She said, ‘My father invites you to reward you for having watered our sheep for us.’ This is polite in the expression; she did not make an absolute request so as not to suggest suspicion. Rather, she said, My father invites you to reward you for having watered our sheep for us, meaning to reward you and recompense you for having watered our sheep. So when he came to him and related to him the story, that is, he mentioned to him what had happened to him and the reason for which he had left his country, “he said, ‘Do not fear. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.’” He said, “Be at peace and be content, for you have left their kingdom, for they have no power in our country.” That is why he said, You have escaped from the wrongdoing people. The commentators differed about who this man was. Some say that he was the Prophet Shuaib, peace be upon him, who was sent to the people of Madyan. This is the well-known view among many scholars. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others also said this. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Abdul Aziz Al-Awsi told us, Malik bin Anas told us that he heard that Shuaib was the one to whom Moses told the story. He said, Do not fear, you have been saved from the wrongdoing people. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Salamah bin Sa'd Al-Ghazi that he visited the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said to him, Welcome to the people of Shuaib and the two sisters of Moses, you have been guided. Others said, Rather, he was the nephew of Shuaib. It was also said that he was a believing man from the people of Shuaib. Still others said, "Shuaib lived a long time before the time of Moses, peace be upon him, because he said to his people, 'The people of Lot are not far from you.'" The destruction of the people of Lot occurred during the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, according to the text of the Quran. It is known that there was a long period of more than four hundred years between Abraham and Moses, peace be upon them, as mentioned by more than one person. What is said that Shu`ayb lived for a long time is - and God knows best - a precaution against this problem. What strengthens the fact that he was not Shu`ayb is that if he was him, his name would have been mentioned in the Qur’an here. What is mentioned in some hadiths that explicitly mention him in the story of Moses is not authentically attributed to them, as we will mention soon, God willing. What is found in the books of the Children of Israel is that this man’s name was Thiron, and God knows best. Abu Ubaidah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas`ud said: Thiron is the nephew of Shu`ayb, peace be upon him. And on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The one whom Moses hired to enrich the ruler of Midian. Ibn Jarir narrated it with this chain of transmission. Then he said: The correct view is that this can only be understood through a report, and there is no report that can be used as evidence in this regard. God the Almighty said: “One of the two daughters said, ‘O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.’” That is, one of the two daughters of this man said. It was said that she was the one who went behind Moses, peace be upon him. She said to her father, O my father, hire him, meaning to tend these sheep. Umar, Ibn Abbas, Shuraih al-Qadi, Abu Malik, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others said: When she said, Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy, her father said to her, And how do you know that? She said to him, “He lifted a rock that only ten men could lift, and when I came with him, I went ahead of him, and he said to me, ‘Stand behind me, and if the road differs from my side, throw me a pebble so that I may know the way and find my way to him.’” Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Masoud - who said: The three most discerning people are: Abu Bakr when he discerned Umar; the companion of Joseph when he said, Make his stay honorable; and the companion of Moses when she said, “O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.” He said, Indeed, I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine. That is, this old man asked him to tend his sheep and marry him to one of his two daughters. Shuaib al-Jubba’i said: They were Safuriya and Sharaf, and it is said that they were Liya. The companions of Abu Hanifa used this verse as evidence for the validity of a sale if someone says, I have sold you one of these two slaves for one hundred, and he says, I have bought, that it is valid, and God knows best. And his saying: “On condition that you hire me for eight years. If you complete ten, then it is from you” meaning that you tend my sheep for eight years. If you volunteer two more years, then it is yours, otherwise eight is sufficient. “And I do not want to make it difficult for you. You will find me, if God wills, among the righteous” meaning that I will not make it difficult for you, nor will I harm you, nor will I argue with you. They used this noble verse as evidence for the school of thought of Al-Awza’i, that if he said: I sold this to you for ten in cash or twenty on credit, then it is valid, and the buyer chooses whichever he takes, it is valid. The hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud, Whoever sells two sales in one sale, he has the better of them or the interest is based on this school of thought. There is some consideration in using this verse and this hadith as evidence for this school of thought, but this is not the place to elaborate on it due to its length. And God knows best. Then the companions of Imam Ahmad and those who followed them in the validity of hiring a worker for food and clothing, used this verse as evidence, and they relied on what Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah narrated in his book Al-Sunan where he said: Chapter on hiring a worker for food and clothing, Muhammad bin Al-Himsi told us, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Muslimah bin Ali, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Mundhir Al-Sulami say: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited Ta Seen Meem until he reached the story of Moses, he said: Indeed, Moses hired himself for eight or ten years in exchange for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach. This hadith is weak from this source, because Muslimah bin Ali, who is Al-Khashani Al-Dimashqi Al-Balati, is a weak narrator according to the imams, but it has been narrated from another source, and there is also doubt about it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Sufyan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Nadr Al-Sulami, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, peace be upon him, hired himself out for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach.” And the Almighty’s statement, informing about Moses, peace be upon him: “He said, ‘This is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no transgression against me. And God is Witness over what we say.’” He said: Moses said to his son-in-law: The matter is as you said, that you hired me for eight years. If I complete ten, then it is from me. So when I fulfill the lesser of the two terms, I have been released from the covenant and released from the condition. For this reason, he said: Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no transgression against me, meaning there is no blame on me, even though the full term, although it is permissible, is still in excess from another aspect, based on external evidence, as God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: But whoever hastens to complete it within two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: To Hamza bin Amr Al-Aslami, may God be pleased with him, who fasted a lot, and he asked him about fasting while traveling, so he said: If you wish, then fast, and if you wish, then break your fast, even though the act of fasting is more likely based on other evidence. This evidence indicates that Moses, peace be upon him, only did the most complete and perfect of the two terms. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, Marwan bin Shuja’ told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A Jew from the people of Al-Hirah asked me: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? So I said: I do not know until I go to the scholar of the Arabs and ask him. So I went to Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and asked him. He said: He fulfilled most of them and the best of them. When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, he does. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it, and this is how Hakim bin Jubair and others narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. It was mentioned in the Hadith of Al-Fitun, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: The one who asked him was a Christian man, and the first is more likely, and God knows best. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Tusi told us, Al-Humaidi told us, Sufyan told us, Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Ya’qub told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I asked Gabriel: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: He completed and perfected them.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Humaidi, on the authority of Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah: Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Ya’qub told me, and he was of my age or younger than me, and he mentioned it. There is an inaccuracy in its chain of transmission, and this Ibrahim is not well-known. Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abaan al-Qurashi, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn A'yan, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He then mentioned it and said: We do not know of it as having been transmitted from Ibn Abbas except through this chain of transmission. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Yunus bin Abdul A’la, Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr bin Al-Harith informed us, on the authority of Yahya bin Maymun Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Yusuf bin Tirh, “The Messenger of God was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: I have no knowledge. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, and Gabriel said: I have no knowledge. So Gabriel asked an angel above him, and he said: I have no knowledge. So that angel asked his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, about what Gabriel had asked him, about what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had asked him. So the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, said: He fulfilled the more righteous and lasting of the two, or he said the purest of the two.” This is a mursal, but it has been transmitted in a mursal form from another source. Sunayd said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: I will ask Israfil, so he asked him, and he said: I will ask the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, so he asked him, and He said: The more righteous and fulfilling of the two.” Another chain of transmission also transmitted Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abu Ma’shar narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more fulfilling and complete of them. These chains of transmission are mutually supportive. This has also been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) from the narration of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abu Ubaidullah Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sakn narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Idris narrated to us, Uwaidh ibn Abi Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more fulfilling and complete of them. He said: “And if you are asked: Which of the two women did he marry? Say: The younger of the two.” Al-Bazzar then said: We do not know of it being narrated from Abu Dharr except with this chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ubadh ibn Abi Imran, and he is weak. Then, a similar hadith was narrated from Utbah ibn al-Nadr with a very strange addition. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Sijistani told us, Yahya ibn Bakir told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, al-Harith ibn Yazid told us on the authority of Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah ibn al-Nadr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more righteous and fulfilling of the two. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When Moses, peace be upon him, wanted to leave Shu’ayb, peace be upon him, he ordered his wife to ask her father to give her enough from his sheep to live on. So he gave her what his sheep had given birth to that year of all colors. He said: Not a single sheep passed by without Moses striking its side with his staff, and it gave birth to all colors, and two or three, each sheep having no spots, no blemishes, no frills that would escape the hand, and no blemishes.” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you conquer Syria, you will find remnants of it, and they are the Samaritans. This is how al-Bazzar reported it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in a more detailed manner than this, saying: Abu Zur’ah told us, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Bakir told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told me H and Abu Zur’ah told us, Safwan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Hadrami on the authority of Ali bin Rabah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Nadr Al-Sulami, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, peace be upon him, hired himself for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach. When he fulfilled the term, it was said: O Messenger of God, which of the two terms is better? He said: The more righteous and the more fulfilled. When he wanted to leave Shu’aib, he ordered his wife to ask her father to give her from his sheep what they would live on, so he gave her what his sheep had given birth to of different colors from the offspring of that year, and his sheep were black and beautiful. Moses, peace be upon him, went to his staff, named it from the end, then put it at the bottom of the basin, then brought it to drink. Moses stood in front of the pool and not a single sheep came out of it except that he struck its side with a sheep. He said: “So it gave birth and gave birth and all of them were of different colors except one or two sheep that had no spots.” Yahya said: Not a lizard. Safwan said: Not a monitor lizard. Abu Zur’ah said: The correct one is a hyena, not a fox, not a fox, not a hyena that could pass the hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you were to conquer Syria, you would find the remains of those sheep, and they are the Samaritans. Abu Zur’ah narrated to us, Safwan told us: I heard Al-Walid say: I asked Ibn Lahi’ah what is a fashoosh? He said: It is the one that gushes forth its milk and has a wide mouth. I said: What is a lizard? He said: It is the one with a long udder that drags it. I said: What is an azouz? He said: It is the one with a narrow mouth. I said: What is a thawul? He said: It is the one that has no udder except in the form of two nipples. I said: What is a kameeshah? He said: It is the one that misses the hand, the kameeshah of the udder is small and cannot be grasped by the hand. This hadith is narrated by Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah Al-Misri, and his memory is poor, and I fear that it may be attributed to the Prophet in error, and God knows best. It should be narrated that there is no fushuh in it, nor azouz, nor dhuboob, nor tha’ool, nor kameeshah, to mention every deficient characteristic with its corresponding deficient characteristics. Ibn Jarir narrated from the words of Anas bin Malik, with a chain of transmission that is almost complete, so he said: Muhammad bin al-Muthanna told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told us, Qatadah told us, Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, told us: When the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, called his companion to the appointed time between them, his companion said to him: Every ewe that gives birth to a color other than its own, its offspring is yours. So Moses raised ropes over the water, and when they saw the ghost, they were startled, so they wandered around, and they all gave birth to spotted ones except one ewe, and all of their offspring were lost that year.
28:26: When the two women quickly returned with the sheep to their father, he was dismayed by their quick arrival. He asked them about their situation, and they told him what Moses had done. He sent one of them to invite him to her father. God the Almighty said: Then one of them came to him walking shyly, meaning the gait of a free woman, as narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Omar may God be pleased with him, who said: She was hiding behind the sleeve of her armor. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Nu'aym told us, Isra'il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: Omar may God be pleased with him said: She came walking shyly, holding her garment over her face, not a slutty woman, neither a coquettish nor a slut. This is a sound chain of transmission. Al-Jawhari said: The salafi' is a bold man, a strong-willed woman, and a strong camel. She said, ‘My father invites you to reward you for having watered our sheep for us.’ This is polite in the expression; she did not make an absolute request so as not to suggest suspicion. Rather, she said, My father invites you to reward you for having watered our sheep for us, meaning to reward you and recompense you for having watered our sheep. So when he came to him and related to him the story, that is, he mentioned to him what had happened to him and the reason for which he had left his country, “he said, ‘Do not fear. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.’” He said, “Be at peace and be content, for you have left their kingdom, for they have no power in our country.” That is why he said, You have escaped from the wrongdoing people. The commentators differed about who this man was. Some say that he was the Prophet Shuaib, peace be upon him, who was sent to the people of Madyan. This is the well-known view among many scholars. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others also said this. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Abdul Aziz Al-Awsi told us, Malik bin Anas told us that he heard that Shuaib was the one to whom Moses told the story. He said, Do not fear, you have been saved from the wrongdoing people. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Salamah bin Sa'd Al-Ghazi that he visited the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said to him, Welcome to the people of Shuaib and the two sisters of Moses, you have been guided. Others said, Rather, he was the nephew of Shuaib. It was also said that he was a believing man from the people of Shuaib. Still others said, "Shuaib lived a long time before the time of Moses, peace be upon him, because he said to his people, 'The people of Lot are not far from you.'" The destruction of the people of Lot occurred during the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, according to the text of the Quran. It is known that there was a long period of more than four hundred years between Abraham and Moses, peace be upon them, as mentioned by more than one person. What is said that Shu`ayb lived for a long time is - and God knows best - a precaution against this problem. What strengthens the fact that he was not Shu`ayb is that if he was him, his name would have been mentioned in the Qur’an here. What is mentioned in some hadiths that explicitly mention him in the story of Moses is not authentically attributed to them, as we will mention soon, God willing. What is found in the books of the Children of Israel is that this man’s name was Thiron, and God knows best. Abu Ubaidah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas`ud said: Thiron is the nephew of Shu`ayb, peace be upon him. And on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The one whom Moses hired to enrich the ruler of Midian. Ibn Jarir narrated it with this chain of transmission. Then he said: The correct view is that this can only be understood through a report, and there is no report that can be used as evidence in this regard. God the Almighty said: “One of the two daughters said, ‘O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.’” That is, one of the two daughters of this man said. It was said that she was the one who went behind Moses, peace be upon him. She said to her father, O my father, hire him, meaning to tend these sheep. Umar, Ibn Abbas, Shuraih al-Qadi, Abu Malik, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others said: When she said, Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy, her father said to her, And how do you know that? She said to him, “He lifted a rock that only ten men could lift, and when I came with him, I went ahead of him, and he said to me, ‘Stand behind me, and if the road differs from my side, throw me a pebble so that I may know the way and find my way to him.’” Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Masoud - who said: The three most discerning people are: Abu Bakr when he discerned Umar; the companion of Joseph when he said, Make his stay honorable; and the companion of Moses when she said, “O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.” He said, Indeed, I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine. That is, this old man asked him to tend his sheep and marry him to one of his two daughters. Shuaib al-Jubba’i said: They were Safuriya and Sharaf, and it is said that they were Liya. The companions of Abu Hanifa used this verse as evidence for the validity of a sale if someone says, I have sold you one of these two slaves for one hundred, and he says, I have bought, that it is valid, and God knows best. And his saying: “On condition that you hire me for eight years. If you complete ten, then it is from you” meaning that you tend my sheep for eight years. If you volunteer two more years, then it is yours, otherwise eight is sufficient. “And I do not want to make it difficult for you. You will find me, if God wills, among the righteous” meaning that I will not make it difficult for you, nor will I harm you, nor will I argue with you. They used this noble verse as evidence for the school of thought of Al-Awza’i, that if he said: I sold this to you for ten in cash or twenty on credit, then it is valid, and the buyer chooses whichever he takes, it is valid. The hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud, Whoever sells two sales in one sale, he has the better of them or the interest is based on this school of thought. There is some consideration in using this verse and this hadith as evidence for this school of thought, but this is not the place to elaborate on it due to its length. And God knows best. Then the companions of Imam Ahmad and those who followed them in the validity of hiring a worker for food and clothing, used this verse as evidence, and they relied on what Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah narrated in his book Al-Sunan where he said: Chapter on hiring a worker for food and clothing, Muhammad bin Al-Himsi told us, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Muslimah bin Ali, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Mundhir Al-Sulami say: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited Ta Seen Meem until he reached the story of Moses, he said: Indeed, Moses hired himself for eight or ten years in exchange for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach. This hadith is weak from this source, because Muslimah bin Ali, who is Al-Khashani Al-Dimashqi Al-Balati, is a weak narrator according to the imams, but it has been narrated from another source, and there is also doubt about it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Sufyan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Nadr Al-Sulami, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, peace be upon him, hired himself out for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach.” And the Almighty’s statement, informing about Moses, peace be upon him: “He said, ‘This is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no transgression against me. And God is Witness over what we say.’” He said: Moses said to his son-in-law: The matter is as you said, that you hired me for eight years. If I complete ten, then it is from me. So when I fulfill the lesser of the two terms, I have been released from the covenant and released from the condition. For this reason, he said: Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no transgression against me, meaning there is no blame on me, even though the full term, although it is permissible, is still in excess from another aspect, based on external evidence, as God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: But whoever hastens to complete it within two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: To Hamza bin Amr Al-Aslami, may God be pleased with him, who fasted a lot, and he asked him about fasting while traveling, so he said: If you wish, then fast, and if you wish, then break your fast, even though the act of fasting is more likely based on other evidence. This evidence indicates that Moses, peace be upon him, only did the most complete and perfect of the two terms. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, Marwan bin Shuja’ told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A Jew from the people of Al-Hirah asked me: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? So I said: I do not know until I go to the scholar of the Arabs and ask him. So I went to Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and asked him. He said: He fulfilled most of them and the best of them. When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, he does. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it, and this is how Hakim bin Jubair and others narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. It was mentioned in the Hadith of Al-Fitun, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: The one who asked him was a Christian man, and the first is more likely, and God knows best. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Tusi told us, Al-Humaidi told us, Sufyan told us, Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Ya’qub told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I asked Gabriel: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: He completed and perfected them.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Humaidi, on the authority of Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah: Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Ya’qub told me, and he was of my age or younger than me, and he mentioned it. There is an inaccuracy in its chain of transmission, and this Ibrahim is not well-known. Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abaan al-Qurashi, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn A'yan, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He then mentioned it and said: We do not know of it as having been transmitted from Ibn Abbas except through this chain of transmission. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Yunus bin Abdul A’la, Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr bin Al-Harith informed us, on the authority of Yahya bin Maymun Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Yusuf bin Tirh, “The Messenger of God was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: I have no knowledge. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, and Gabriel said: I have no knowledge. So Gabriel asked an angel above him, and he said: I have no knowledge. So that angel asked his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, about what Gabriel had asked him, about what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had asked him. So the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, said: He fulfilled the more righteous and lasting of the two, or he said the purest of the two.” This is a mursal, but it has been transmitted in a mursal form from another source. Sunayd said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: I will ask Israfil, so he asked him, and he said: I will ask the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, so he asked him, and He said: The more righteous and fulfilling of the two.” Another chain of transmission also transmitted Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abu Ma’shar narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more fulfilling and complete of them. These chains of transmission are mutually supportive. This has also been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) from the narration of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abu Ubaidullah Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sakn narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Idris narrated to us, Uwaidh ibn Abi Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more fulfilling and complete of them. He said: “And if you are asked: Which of the two women did he marry? Say: The younger of the two.” Al-Bazzar then said: We do not know of it being narrated from Abu Dharr except with this chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ubadh ibn Abi Imran, and he is weak. Then, a similar hadith was narrated from Utbah ibn al-Nadr with a very strange addition. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Sijistani told us, Yahya ibn Bakir told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, al-Harith ibn Yazid told us on the authority of Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah ibn al-Nadr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more righteous and fulfilling of the two. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When Moses, peace be upon him, wanted to leave Shu’ayb, peace be upon him, he ordered his wife to ask her father to give her enough from his sheep to live on. So he gave her what his sheep had given birth to that year of all colors. He said: Not a single sheep passed by without Moses striking its side with his staff, and it gave birth to all colors, and two or three, each sheep having no spots, no blemishes, no frills that would escape the hand, and no blemishes.” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you conquer Syria, you will find remnants of it, and they are the Samaritans. This is how al-Bazzar reported it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in a more detailed manner than this, saying: Abu Zur’ah told us, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Bakir told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told me H and Abu Zur’ah told us, Safwan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Hadrami on the authority of Ali bin Rabah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Nadr Al-Sulami, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, peace be upon him, hired himself for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach. When he fulfilled the term, it was said: O Messenger of God, which of the two terms is better? He said: The more righteous and the more fulfilled. When he wanted to leave Shu’aib, he ordered his wife to ask her father to give her from his sheep what they would live on, so he gave her what his sheep had given birth to of different colors from the offspring of that year, and his sheep were black and beautiful. Moses, peace be upon him, went to his staff, named it from the end, then put it at the bottom of the basin, then brought it to drink. Moses stood in front of the pool and not a single sheep came out of it except that he struck its side with a sheep. He said: “So it gave birth and gave birth and all of them were of different colors except one or two sheep that had no spots.” Yahya said: Not a lizard. Safwan said: Not a monitor lizard. Abu Zur’ah said: The correct one is a hyena, not a fox, not a fox, not a hyena that could pass the hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you were to conquer Syria, you would find the remains of those sheep, and they are the Samaritans. Abu Zur’ah narrated to us, Safwan told us: I heard Al-Walid say: I asked Ibn Lahi’ah what is a fashoosh? He said: It is the one that gushes forth its milk and has a wide mouth. I said: What is a lizard? He said: It is the one with a long udder that drags it. I said: What is an azouz? He said: It is the one with a narrow mouth. I said: What is a thawul? He said: It is the one that has no udder except in the form of two nipples. I said: What is a kameeshah? He said: It is the one that misses the hand, the kameeshah of the udder is small and cannot be grasped by the hand. It was mentioned in the Hadith of Al-Fitun, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: The one who asked him was a Christian man, and the first is more likely, and God knows best. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Tusi told us, Al-Humaidi told us, Sufyan told us, Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Ya’qub told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I asked Gabriel: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: He completed and perfected them.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Humaidi, on the authority of Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah: Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Ya’qub told me, and he was of my age or younger than me, and he mentioned it. There is an inaccuracy in its chain of transmission, and this Ibrahim is not well-known. Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abaan al-Qurashi, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn A'yan, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He then mentioned it and said: We do not know of it as having been transmitted from Ibn Abbas except through this chain of transmission. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Yunus bin Abdul A’la, Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr bin Al-Harith informed us, on the authority of Yahya bin Maymun Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Yusuf bin Tirh, “The Messenger of God was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: I have no knowledge. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, and Gabriel said: I have no knowledge. So Gabriel asked an angel above him, and he said: I have no knowledge. So that angel asked his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, about what Gabriel had asked him, about what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had asked him. So the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, said: He fulfilled the more righteous and lasting of the two, or he said the purest of the two.” This is a mursal, but it has been transmitted in a mursal form from another source. Sunayd said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: I will ask Israfil, so he asked him, and he said: I will ask the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, so he asked him, and He said: The more righteous and fulfilling of the two.” Another chain of transmission also transmitted Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abu Ma’shar narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more fulfilling and complete of them. These chains of transmission are mutually supportive. This has also been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) from the narration of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abu Ubaidullah Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sakn narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Idris narrated to us, Uwaidh ibn Abi Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more fulfilling and complete of them. He said: “And if you are asked: Which of the two women did he marry? Say: The younger of the two.” Al-Bazzar then said: We do not know of it being narrated from Abu Dharr except with this chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ubadh ibn Abi Imran, and he is weak. Then, a similar hadith was narrated from Utbah ibn al-Nadr with a very strange addition. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Sijistani told us, Yahya ibn Bakir told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, al-Harith ibn Yazid told us on the authority of Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah ibn al-Nadr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more righteous and fulfilling of the two. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When Moses, peace be upon him, wanted to leave Shu’ayb, peace be upon him, he ordered his wife to ask her father to give her enough from his sheep to live on. So he gave her what his sheep had given birth to that year of all colors. He said: Not a single sheep passed by without Moses striking its side with his staff, and it gave birth to all colors, and two or three, each sheep having no spots, no blemishes, no frills that would escape the hand, and no blemishes.” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you conquer Syria, you will find remnants of it, and they are the Samaritans. This is how al-Bazzar reported it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in a more detailed manner than this, saying: Abu Zur’ah told us, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Bakir told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told me H and Abu Zur’ah told us, Safwan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Hadrami on the authority of Ali bin Rabah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Nadr Al-Sulami, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, peace be upon him, hired himself for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach. When he fulfilled the term, it was said: O Messenger of God, which of the two terms is better? He said: The more righteous and the more fulfilled. When he wanted to leave Shu’aib, he ordered his wife to ask her father to give her from his sheep what they would live on, so he gave her what his sheep had given birth to of different colors from the offspring of that year, and his sheep were black and beautiful. Moses, peace be upon him, went to his staff, named it from the end, then put it at the bottom of the basin, then brought it to drink. Moses stood in front of the pool and not a single sheep came out of it except that he struck its side with a sheep. He said: “So it gave birth and gave birth and all of them were of different colors except one or two sheep that had no spots.” Yahya said: Not a lizard. Safwan said: Not a monitor lizard. Abu Zur’ah said: The correct one is a hyena, not a fox, not a fox, not a hyena that could pass the hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you were to conquer Syria, you would find the remains of those sheep, and they are the Samaritans. Abu Zur’ah narrated to us, Safwan told us: I heard Al-Walid say: I asked Ibn Lahi’ah what is a fashoosh? He said: It is the one that gushes forth its milk and has a wide mouth. I said: What is a lizard? He said: It is the one with a long udder that drags it. I said: What is an azouz? He said: It is the one with a narrow mouth. I said: What is a thawul? He said: It is the one that has no udder except in the form of two nipples. I said: What is a kameeshah? He said: It is the one that misses the hand, the kameeshah of the udder is small and cannot be grasped by the hand. This hadith is narrated by Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah Al-Misri, and his memory is poor, and I fear that it may be attributed to the Prophet in error, and God knows best. It should be narrated that there is no fushuh in it, nor azouz, nor dhuboob, nor tha’ool, nor kameeshah, to mention every deficient characteristic with its corresponding deficient characteristics. Ibn Jarir narrated from the words of Anas bin Malik, with a chain of transmission that is almost complete, so he said: Muhammad bin al-Muthanna told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told us, Qatadah told us, Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, told us: When the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, called his companion to the appointed time between them, his companion said to him: Every ewe that gives birth to a color other than its own, its offspring is yours. So Moses raised ropes over the water, and when they saw the ghost, they were startled, so they wandered around, and they all gave birth to spotted ones except one ewe, and all of their offspring were lost that year.
28:28: When the two women quickly returned with the sheep to their father, he was dismayed by their quick arrival. He asked them about their situation, and they told him what Moses had done. He sent one of them to invite him to her father. God the Almighty said: "Then one of them came to him walking shyly," meaning the gait of a free woman, as narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Omar may God be pleased with him, who said: She was hiding behind the sleeve of her armor. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Nu'aym told us, Isra'il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: Omar may God be pleased with him said: She came walking shyly, holding her garment over her face, not a slutty woman, neither a coquettish nor a slut. This is a sound chain of transmission. Al-Jawhari said: The salafi' is a bold man, a strong-willed woman, and a strong camel. She said, ‘My father invites you to reward you for having watered our sheep for us.’ This is polite in the expression; she did not make an absolute request so as not to suggest suspicion. Rather, she said, My father invites you to reward you for having watered our sheep for us, meaning to reward you and recompense you for having watered our sheep. So when he came to him and related to him the story, that is, he mentioned to him what had happened to him and the reason for which he had left his country, “he said, ‘Do not fear. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.’” He said, “Be at peace and be content, for you have left their kingdom, for they have no power in our country.” That is why he said, You have escaped from the wrongdoing people. The commentators differed about who this man was. Some say that he was the Prophet Shuaib, peace be upon him, who was sent to the people of Madyan. This is the well-known view among many scholars. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others also said this. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Abdul Aziz Al-Awsi told us, Malik bin Anas told us that he heard that Shuaib was the one to whom Moses told the story. He said, "Do not fear, you have been saved from the wrongdoing people." Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Salamah bin Sa'd Al-Ghazi that he visited the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said to him, "Welcome to the people of Shuaib and the two sisters of Moses, you have been guided. Others said, Rather, he was the nephew of Shuaib." It was also said that he was a believing man from the people of Shuaib. Still others said, "Shuaib lived a long time before the time of Moses, peace be upon him, because he said to his people, 'The people of Lot are not far from you.'" The destruction of the people of Lot occurred during the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, according to the text of the Quran. It is known that there was a long period of more than four hundred years between Abraham and Moses, peace be upon them, as mentioned by more than one person. What is said that Shu`ayb lived for a long time is - and God knows best - a precaution against this problem. What strengthens the fact that he was not Shu`ayb is that if he was him, his name would have been mentioned in the Qur’an here. What is mentioned in some hadiths that explicitly mention him in the story of Moses is not authentically attributed to them, as we will mention soon, God willing. What is found in the books of the Children of Israel is that this man’s name was Thiron, and God knows best. Abu Ubaidah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas`ud said: Thiron is the nephew of Shu`ayb, peace be upon him. And on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The one whom Moses hired to enrich the ruler of Midian. Ibn Jarir narrated it with this chain of transmission. Then he said: The correct view is that this can only be understood through a report, and there is no report that can be used as evidence in this regard. God the Almighty said: “One of the two daughters said, ‘O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.’” That is, one of the two daughters of this man said. It was said that she was the one who went behind Moses, peace be upon him. She said to her father, O my father, hire him, meaning to tend these sheep. Umar, Ibn Abbas, Shuraih al-Qadi, Abu Malik, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others said: When she said, Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy, her father said to her, And how do you know that? She said to him, “He lifted a rock that only ten men could lift, and when I came with him, I went ahead of him, and he said to me, ‘Stand behind me, and if the road differs from my side, throw me a pebble so that I may know the way and find my way to him.’” Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Masoud - who said: The three most discerning people are: Abu Bakr when he discerned Umar; the companion of Joseph when he said, Make his stay honorable; and the companion of Moses when she said, “O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.” He said, Indeed, I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine. That is, this old man asked him to tend his sheep and marry him to one of his two daughters. Shuaib al-Jubba’i said: They were Safuriya and Sharaf, and it is said that they were Liya. The companions of Abu Hanifa used this verse as evidence for the validity of a sale if someone says, I have sold you one of these two slaves for one hundred, and he says, I have bought, that it is valid, and God knows best. And his saying: “On condition that you hire me for eight years. If you complete ten, then it is from you” meaning that you tend my sheep for eight years. If you volunteer two more years, then it is yours, otherwise eight is sufficient. “And I do not want to make it difficult for you. You will find me, if God wills, among the righteous” meaning that I will not make it difficult for you, nor will I harm you, nor will I argue with you. They used this noble verse as evidence for the school of thought of Al-Awza’i, that if he said: I sold this to you for ten in cash or twenty on credit, then it is valid, and the buyer chooses whichever he takes, it is valid. The hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud, Whoever sells two sales in one sale, he has the better of them or the interest is based on this school of thought. There is some consideration in using this verse and this hadith as evidence for this school of thought, but this is not the place to elaborate on it due to its length. And God knows best. Then the companions of Imam Ahmad and those who followed them in the validity of hiring a worker for food and clothing, used this verse as evidence, and they relied on what Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah narrated in his book Al-Sunan where he said: Chapter on hiring a worker for food and clothing, Muhammad bin Al-Himsi told us, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Muslimah bin Ali, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Mundhir Al-Sulami say: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited Ta Seen Meem until he reached the story of Moses, he said: Indeed, Moses hired himself for eight or ten years in exchange for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach. This hadith is weak from this source, because Muslimah bin Ali, who is Al-Khashani Al-Dimashqi Al-Balati, is a weak narrator according to the imams, but it has been narrated from another source, and there is also doubt about it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Sufyan told us, Al-Walid told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah bin Al-Nadr Al-Sulami, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, peace be upon him, hired himself out for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his stomach.” And the Almighty’s statement, informing about Moses, peace be upon him: “He said, ‘This is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no transgression against me. And God is Witness over what we say.’” He said: Moses said to his son-in-law: The matter is as you said, that you hired me for eight years. If I complete ten, then it is from me. So when I fulfill the lesser of the two terms, I have been released from the covenant and released from the condition. For this reason, he said: Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no transgression against me, meaning there is no blame on me, even though the full term, although it is permissible, is still in excess from another aspect, based on external evidence, as God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: But whoever hastens to complete it within two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: To Hamza bin Amr Al-Aslami, may God be pleased with him, who fasted a lot, and he asked him about fasting while traveling, so he said: If you wish, then fast, and if you wish, then break your fast, even though the act of fasting is more likely based on other evidence. This evidence indicates that Moses, peace be upon him, only did the most complete and perfect of the two terms. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, Marwan bin Shuja’ told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A Jew from the people of Al-Hirah asked me: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? So I said: I do not know until I go to the scholar of the Arabs and ask him. So I went to Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and asked him. He said: He fulfilled most of them and the best of them. When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, he does. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it, and this is how Hakim bin Jubair and others narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. It was mentioned in the Hadith of Al-Fitun, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: The one who asked him was a Christian man, and the first is more likely, and God knows best. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Tusi told us, Al-Humaidi told us, Sufyan told us, Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Ya’qub told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I asked Gabriel: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: He completed and perfected them.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Humaidi, on the authority of Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah: Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Abi Ya’qub told me, and he was of my age or younger than me, and he mentioned it. There is an inaccuracy in its chain of transmission, and this Ibrahim is not well-known. Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abaan al-Qurashi, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn A'yan, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He then mentioned it and said: We do not know of it as having been transmitted from Ibn Abbas except through this chain of transmission. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Yunus bin Abdul A’la, Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr bin Al-Harith informed us, on the authority of Yahya bin Maymun Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Yusuf bin Tirh, “The Messenger of God was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: I have no knowledge. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, and Gabriel said: I have no knowledge. So Gabriel asked an angel above him, and he said: I have no knowledge. So that angel asked his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, about what Gabriel had asked him, about what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had asked him. So the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, said: He fulfilled the more righteous and lasting of the two, or he said the purest of the two.” This is a mursal, but it has been transmitted in a mursal form from another source. Sunayd said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: I will ask Israfil, so he asked him, and he said: I will ask the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, so he asked him, and He said: The more righteous and fulfilling of the two.” Another chain of transmission also transmitted Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abu Ma’shar narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more fulfilling and complete of them. These chains of transmission are mutually supportive. This has also been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) from the narration of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abu Ubaidullah Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sakn narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Idris narrated to us, Uwaidh ibn Abi Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The more fulfilling and complete of them. He said: “And if you are asked: Which of the two women did he marry? Say: The younger of the two.” Al-Bazzar then said: We do not know of it being narrated from Abu Dharr except with this chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ubadh ibn Abi Imran, and he is weak. Then, a similar hadith was narrated from Utbah ibn al-Nadr with a very strange addition. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Sijistani told us, Yahya ibn Bakir told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, al-Harith ibn Yazid told us on the authority of Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utbah ibn al-Nadr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? 28:29: It was previously mentioned in the interpretation of the previous verse that Moses, peace be upon him, had completed the more complete of the two terms, fulfilled them, was more righteous, perfected them, and was more pious. This may also be understood from the noble verse where God Almighty says: And when Moses had completed the term, meaning the more complete of the two, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: He completed ten years, and after that, ten more. I have not seen this statement attributed to anyone other than him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it on his authority, and God knows best. And his saying: And he traveled with his family. They said: Moses had longed for his country and his family, so he decided to visit them secretly from Pharaoh and his people. He took his family and the sheep that he had with him, which his son-in-law had given him. He traveled with them on a cold, dark, rainy night. He stopped at a place, and whenever he lit his fire, it did not light anything. He was amazed by that, and while he was like that, he perceived a fire on the side of the mountain, meaning he saw a fire lighting up in the distance. “So he said to his family, ‘Stay here, for I have perceived a fire,’ meaning until I go to it. “Perhaps I can bring you some information from it,” because he had lost his way. Or a burning ember from the fire, meaning a piece of it. Perhaps you may warm yourselves from the cold. God Almighty said: And when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, meaning from the side of the valley, which is next to the mountain on his right, from the western side, as God Almighty said: And you were not on the western side when We decreed the matter to Moses. This is one of the things that indicates that Moses intended the fire. Some of the People of the Book say that it is a bramble tree. Qatadah said: It is a bramble tree, and his staff is a bramble tree. 28:35: When God Almighty commanded him to go to Pharaoh, who had only left Egypt to flee from him and fear his power, He said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have killed one of them’ meaning the Copt and I fear that they will kill me meaning if they see me and my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I in speech. This is because Moses, peace be upon him, had a lisp in his tongue because of what he had taken of that live coal when he was given the choice between it and a date or a pearl, so he took the live coal and placed it on his tongue, and he had difficulty in expressing himself. For this reason he said: And untie the knot from my tongue * that they may understand my speech * and appoint for me a helper from my family * Aaron, my brother * strengthen me through him * and let him share in my task meaning that he would comfort me in what you commanded me to do of this great position, which is to carry out the burdens of prophethood and the message to this arrogant, tyrannical, stubborn king. For this reason he said: And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I in speech, so send him with me as a support meaning a helper, supporter, and strengthener For my sake, believe me in what I say and report on the authority of God Almighty, because the report of two people is more effective in the souls than the report of one person, and for this reason he said: I fear that they will lie. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, A support that will confirm me, meaning that he will explain to them what I am saying to them, for he understands from me what they do not understand. So when Moses asked that, God Almighty said, We will strengthen you with your brother, meaning, We will strengthen your matter and support you with your brother whom you asked to be a prophet with you, as He said in the other verse, Your request has been granted, O Moses. And God Almighty said, And We bestowed upon him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, a prophet. For this reason, some of the early Muslims said, “No one has done more favors to his brother than Moses did to Aaron, peace be upon them both, for he interceded for him until God made him a prophet and messenger with him to Pharaoh and his people. For this reason, God Almighty said about Moses, “And he was esteemed in the sight of God.” And the Almighty’s saying: And We will give you both an authority meaning a compelling argument so they cannot reach you with Our signs meaning they will have no way to harm you because of your conveying the signs of God, as God Almighty said: “O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And God will protect you from the people” and God Almighty said: “Those who convey the messages of God and fear Him and do not fear anyone except God. And sufficient is God as a reckoner” meaning God is sufficient as a supporter, helper, and supporter. For this reason, He informed them that the outcome is for them and for those who follow them in this world and the hereafter, as God Almighty said: You and those who follow you will be the victors as God Almighty said: “God has decreed, ‘I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might’” and God Almighty said: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world to the end of the verse. Ibn Jarir explained that the meaning is: And We will give you both an authority so they cannot reach you, then He begins by saying: With Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the victors meaning you and those who follow you will be the victors. The victors followed you with Our signs. There is no doubt that this meaning is correct, and it is obtained from the first explanation, so there is no need for this, and God knows best.
28:36: God Almighty tells us about the coming of Moses and his brother Aaron to Pharaoh and his people and the presentation of the dazzling miracles that God gave them, and the overwhelming evidence of their truthfulness in what they reported about God Almighty regarding His Oneness and following His commands. When Pharaoh and his people witnessed that and witnessed it and confirmed it, and were certain that it was from God, they turned their disbelief and transgression to stubbornness and boasting, and that was due to their tyranny and arrogance in following the truth, so they said, This is nothing but fabricated magic, meaning contrived and fabricated. They wanted to oppose it with trickery and prestige, but that did not work for them. And His statement: And we have not heard of this among our forefathers, meaning the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him. They say: We have not seen any of our forefathers upon this religion, and we have not seen people except associating other gods with God. So Moses, peace be upon him, said in response to them: My Lord knows best who has brought guidance from Him, meaning from me and from you, and He will judge between me and you. For this reason He said: And whoever will have the final home, meaning victory, triumph, and support, Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed, meaning those who associate partners with God Almighty.

28:38: God Almighty tells about Pharaoh's disbelief, his tyranny and his slander in his ugly claim to divinity for himself, may God curse him, as God Almighty said: So he deceived his people and they obeyed him [verse]. This is because he called them to acknowledge his divinity, but they responded to him with their weak minds and foolishness. That is why He said: O eminent ones, I do not know of any god for you other than Me. And God Almighty said, informing about him: "So he was gathered and called out. * He said, "I am your highest lord." * So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life]. * Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears." Meaning that he gathered his people and called out to them in his loud voice, declaring that to them, so they responded to him, listening and obeying. That is why God Almighty took revenge on him, making him a lesson for others in this world and the hereafter. He even confronted Moses, the one who spoke to God, with that, and said: If you take a god other than Me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned. And his saying: Then kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay, and make for me a tower that I may look up to the God of Moses. He means that he ordered his minister Haman, the manager of his subjects and advisor of his state, to kindle for him upon the clay, meaning that he would make bricks for him to build the tower, which is the lofty, high palace, as he said in the other verse: “And Pharaoh said, ‘O Haman, construct for me a tower that I may reach the ways * The ways of the heavens and look up to the God of Moses. And indeed, I think he is a liar.’ Thus the evil of his work was made attractive to Pharaoh, and he was averted from the way. And the plot of Pharaoh was nothing but ruin.” That is because Pharaoh built this tower, higher than which no building had been seen in the world. He only wanted by this to show his subjects that Moses was lying in what he claimed of claiming a god other than Pharaoh. For this reason he said: And indeed, I think he is among the liars, meaning in his saying: There is a lord other than me, not that he lied about him in that God Almighty sent him, because he did not acknowledge the existence of the Creator, glory be to Him, for he said: And what is the Lord of the worlds? And he said: If you should take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the The imprisoned ones and said, O assembly, I do not know of any god for you other than me. This is what Ibn Jarir said. And the Almighty said: And he and his soldiers were arrogant upon the earth without right and thought that they would not be returned to Us meaning they transgressed and acted tyrannically, and spread corruption on the earth, and believed that there would be no resurrection or return. “So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment. Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.” That is why the Almighty said here: So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea meaning We drowned them in the sea in a single morning, so not a single one of them remained. “Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers. And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire” meaning for those who followed their path in denying the Messengers and nullifying the Creator. And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be aided meaning the disgrace of this world was combined with the humiliation of the Hereafter, as the Almighty said: We destroyed them, and there is no helper for them. And the Almighty said: And We pursued them in this world with a curse meaning that God prescribed their curse and the curse of their king Pharaoh on the tongues of His believing servants who followed His messengers, just as they are cursed in this world on the tongues of the prophets and their followers as well. And on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised. Qatada said: This verse is like the Almighty’s saying: And they will be pursued in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection - what an evil provision it is.

28:43: God Almighty tells us about the blessings He bestowed upon His servant and messenger Moses, the one who spoke to God, upon him be the best of prayers and peace from his Lord, by sending down the Torah to him after He destroyed Pharaoh and his people. And the Almighty’s saying: After We destroyed the former generations means that after the Torah was revealed, He did not punish a nation in general, but rather He ordered the believers to fight the enemies of God from the polytheists, as God Almighty said: And Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities came with sin, but they disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a terrible grip. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad and Abd al-Wahhab told us, they said: Awf told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: God did not destroy a people with a punishment from the sky or from the earth after the Torah was revealed on the face of the earth, except for the people of the village who were transformed into monkeys after Moses. Then he recited: And We gave Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations and the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Awf ibn Abi Jamila al-A’rabi in a similar manner. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Amr ibn Ali al-Fallas, on the authority of Yahya al-Qattan, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Then he narrated it On the authority of Nasr ibn Ali, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, tracing it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God did not destroy a people with a punishment from the sky or from the earth except before Moses. Then he recited: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations 1:17. And His statement: Insight for the people and guidance and mercy means from blindness and error, and guidance to the truth and mercy, meaning direction to righteous deeds that they may be reminded meaning that perhaps people will remember by it and be guided because of it.
28:44: The Almighty says, pointing out the proof of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he informed him of the past unseen events, as if his listener was a witness behind what preceded, and he was an illiterate man who did not read anything from the books, and he grew up among a people who did not know anything about that. Also, when he informed him about Mary and what happened to her, the Almighty said: And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed verse, meaning, you were not present for that, but God revealed it to you. And likewise when he informed him about Noah and his people, and what happened of God’s saving him and drowning his people, then the Almighty said: “That is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you. You did not know it, nor did your people, before this, so be patient. Indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous” verse. And He said at the end of the surah: “That is from the report of the towns. We relate it to you” verse. And He said after mentioning the story of Joseph: That is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they decided upon their plan while they were plotting verse. And He said in Surah Ta-Ha 20:Thus do We relate to you some of the report of what preceded the verse, and He said here after He told the story of Moses from beginning to end, and how God’s revelation to him and His speaking to him began, And you were not on the western side when We decreed the matter to Moses meaning you were not, O Muhammad, on the western side of the mountain from which God spoke to Moses from the tree that is on the eastern side of the valley, nor were you among the witnesses to that, but God, glory be to Him, revealed that to you, so that it would be an argument and proof against centuries that had passed, and they had forgotten God’s arguments against them and what He revealed to the previous prophets. And the Almighty said: And you were not residing among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses meaning, you were not residing among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses when you informed about their prophet Shuaib and what he said to his people and how they responded to him. But We were messengers meaning, but We revealed that to you and sent you to the people as a messenger. And you were not by the side of the Mount when We called Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa’i said in the interpretation of his Sunan: Ali ibn Hajar informed us, Isa ibn Yunus informed us, on the authority of Hamza al-Zayyat, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ali ibn Mudrik, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him. And you were not by the side of the Mount when We called he said: It was called out to them: O nation of Muhammad, I gave to you before you asked Me, and I answered you before you called upon Me. And this is how Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of a group on the authority of Hamza, who is Ibn Habib al-Zayyat, on the authority of al-A’mash. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Wakee’ and Yahya bin Isa, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ali bin Mudrik, on the authority of Abu Zar’ah, who is the son of Amr bin Jarir, that he said that from his own words, and God knows best. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said, And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called to your nation in the loins of their fathers to believe in you when you were sent. Qatada said, And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called to Moses.
