28:48: God Almighty says, informing about the people who, if He had punished them before the proof was established against them, would have argued that no Messenger had come to them. When the truth came to them from Him through the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said, out of stubbornness, obstinacy, disbelief, ignorance, and atheism, Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given? verse, meaning—and God knows best—many signs such as the staff, the hand, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the reduction of crops and fruits, which would make things difficult for the enemies of God, and the splitting of the sea, the shading of the clouds, the sending down of manna and quails, and other dazzling signs and compelling proofs that God Almighty performed through the hands of Moses, peace be upon him, as proof and evidence for Him against Pharaoh, his people, and the Children of Israel. Despite all of this, it did not work against Pharaoh and his people. Rather, they disbelieved in Moses and his brother Aaron, as they said to them, Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers doing, and so that you may have arrogance in the land? And we are not to believe you.” And God Almighty said: So they denied them both, and they were among the destroyed. That is why He said here: Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? That is, did not mankind disbelieve in what was given to Moses of those great signs? They said, ‘Two magicians who cooperated,’ that is, they cooperated. And they said, ‘Indeed, we are disbelievers in both of them.’ That is, we are disbelievers in both of them. Because of the strong connection, companionship, and similarity between Moses and Aaron, mentioning one of them indicates the other, as the poet said: I do not know if I go to a land seeking goodness, which of the two is more suitable for me? So I do not know whether good or evil will befall me. Mujahid ibn Jabr said: The Jews ordered the Quraysh to say that to Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so God said: {Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, Two magicians who backed up each other.} He said, meaning Moses and Aaron (peace and blessings of God be upon them). Backed up means they cooperated and supported each other and believed each other. This is what Saeed ibn Jubayr and Abu Razin said about His statement, Two magicians, meaning Moses and Aaron. This is a good and strong statement, and God knows best. Muslim ibn Yasar said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They said, “Two magicians who backed up each other. He said: They meant Moses and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon them). This is the narration of Al-Hasan Al-Basri. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It means Jesus and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon them). This is far-fetched because Jesus was not mentioned here, and God knows best. As for the one who reads Two magicians conspired against one another, Ali ibn Abi Talha and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They mean the Torah and the Qur’an. This is what Asim Al-Jundi, Al-Suddi and Abd Al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said. Al-Suddi said: It means that each one of them confirmed the truth of the other. Ikrimah said: They mean the Torah and the Gospel. This is a narration on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, and Ibn Jarir chose this as the preferred opinion. Ad-Dahhak and Qatada said: The Gospel and the Qur’an, and God the Almighty knows best. What appears from the reading of magic is that they mean the Torah and the Qur’an, because He said after it: “Say: Then bring a Book from God that is better guidance than both of them, and I will follow it.” God often pairs the Torah and the Qur’an, as in His statement: “Say: Who sent down the Book which Moses brought, a light and guidance for the people? You make it into sheets, some of which you reveal and much you conceal. And you were taught that which you did not know, neither you nor your fathers. Say: God. Then leave them in their idle talk, playing. And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed.” And He said at the end of the Surah: Then We gave Moses the Scripture, completing it for him who does good. And He said: And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and fear God that you may receive mercy. And the jinn said: Indeed, we have heard a Book sent down after Moses, confirming what was before it. And Waraqa ibn Nawfal said: This is the Law that was sent down to Moses. It is necessary for those with understanding to know that God Almighty did not send down a book from heaven, among the various books He sent down to His prophets, that was more perfect, comprehensive, eloquent, greater, or noble than the book that He sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is the Qur’an. After it in honor and greatness is the book that He sent down to Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him, which is the book about which God said: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for the Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars [as well] by what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, and they were witnesses thereto.” The Gospel was sent down to complement the Torah and to replace some of what was forbidden to the Children of Israel. For this reason, God Almighty said: “Say, ‘Then bring a Book from God that is better guidance than both of them, that I may follow it, if you should be truthful. ’” That is, in what you use to defend the truth and oppose falsehood with, God Almighty said: But if they do not respond to you, That is, if they do not answer what you say to them, and do not follow the truth, then know that they only follow their own desires, That is, without proof or argument. And who is more astray? “Those who follow their desires without guidance from God” meaning without an argument taken from the Book of God Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. And the saying of God the Almighty: {And We have certainly given them the Word} Mujahid said: We have detailed the Word to them. Al-Suddi said: We made the Word clear to them. Qatada said: God the Almighty says: Inform them of how He dealt with those who have passed away, and how He will deal with them, that they may remember. Mujahid and others said: {And We have given them the Word} meaning Quraysh, and this is the apparent meaning, but Hammad ibn Salamah said on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar on the authority of Yahya ibn Ja’dah on the authority of Rifa’ah, this Rifa’ah is Ibn Qaraza Al-Qurazi, and Ibn Mandah made him: Rifa’ah ibn Shamwal, the maternal uncle of Safiyyah bint Huyayy, and he is the one who divorced Tamimah bint Wahb, who was married after him to Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr ibn Bata. This is what Ibn al-Athir mentioned. He said: {And We have certainly given them the Word} was revealed concerning ten, and I am one of them. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim from his hadith.

28:52: God tells us about the learned saints among the People of the Book that they believe in the Qur’an, as He says: Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it with its true recital - those believe in it. And He says: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in God and in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly submissive to God. And He says: “Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration. * And they say, ‘Exalted is our Lord! The promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.’” And He says: “And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, ‘We are Christians.’ That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. * And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.’” Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: It was revealed about seventy priests sent by the Negus. When they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he recited to them “Ya Seen. By the Wise Qur’an” until he finished it. Then they began to cry and submitted to Islam. This other verse was revealed about them: “Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, ‘We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before it, Muslims.’” Meaning, before this Qur’an, we were Muslims, that is, monotheists, sincere to God, and responsive to Him. God the Almighty said: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured. That is, those who are described with this characteristic are those who believed in the first Book and then the second. That is why He said: for what they patiently endured, that is, in following the truth. For enduring such a thing is difficult for the soul. It was reported in the Sahih from the hadith of Amir al-Sha’bi on the authority of Abu Burdah on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Three will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed in his Prophet and then believed in me; a slave who fulfilled the right of God and the right of his masters; and a man who had a female slave, educated her and educated her well, then freed her and married her.” Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq Al-Silhini told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Umamah, who said: I was under the mount of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of the conquest, and he said something good and beautiful, and among what he said was: “Whoever from the People of the Two Books converts to Islam will have his reward twice, and he has what we have and is responsible for what we are responsible for. And whoever from the polytheists converts to Islam will have his reward and he has what we have and is responsible for what we are responsible for.” God the Almighty says: {And they repel evil with good} meaning, they do not respond to evil with the same, but rather they pardon and overlook. {And from what We have provided them they spend} meaning, from what We have provided them from the lawful, they spend on God’s creation, in obligatory expenses for their families and relatives, and the obligatory and recommended zakat, and voluntary charity and acts of worship. God the Almighty says: {And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it} meaning, they do not mix with its people or associate with them, but as God the Almighty says: {And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity}. {And they say, “To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We seek not the ignorant.”} meaning, if a foolish person speaks to them in a way that is not appropriate for them to respond to, they turn away from him and do not respond to him with the same ugly words, and they only speak good words. That is why He said about them that they said, {To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We seek not the ignorant.”} meaning, we do not desire the path of the ignorant, nor do we like it. Muhammad bin Ishaq said in Al-Sirah: Then twenty men or close to that number of Christians came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca, when they heard the report of him from Abyssinia. They found him in the mosque, so they sat with him and spoke to him and asked him questions, and men from Quraysh were in their clubs around the Kaaba. When they finished asking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what they wanted, he called them to God Almighty and recited the Qur’an to them. When they heard the Qur’an, their eyes overflowed with tears, then they responded to God and believed in him and confirmed him, and they recognized from him what was described to them in their book about his affair. When they left him, Abu Jahl bin Hisham intercepted them with a group of Quraysh, and they said to them: May God disappoint you regarding the caravan. He sent you from behind you from the people of your religion to search for them to bring them report of the man, but your gatherings with him did not feel secure until you abandoned your religion and believed him in what he said. He said: We do not know of a caravan more foolish than you, or something like that, so they said to them: Peace be upon you, we do not ignore you. For us is what we are, and for you is what you are. We have not spared ourselves any good. He said: It is said that the Christian group were from Najran, and God knows best which one it was. He said: I asked Al-Zuhri about whom these verses were revealed? He said: I have not ceased to hear from our scholars that they were revealed about the Negus and his companions may God be pleased with them, and the verses in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:“That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. 28:56: God the Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that you, O Muhammad, do not guide whom you love, meaning that is not up to you, but rather the task of conveying the message is your responsibility, and God guides whom He wills, and He has the perfect wisdom and the conclusive proof, as He the Almighty says: It is not up to you to guide them, but God guides whom He wills, and He the Almighty says: And most people, no matter how much you desire it, will not believe. This verse is more specific than all of this, for He says: “Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but God guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided,” meaning He is most knowing of who deserves guidance and who deserves to be led astray. It has been proven in the two Sahihs that it was revealed about Abu Talib, the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he used to protect him, support him, stand by his side, and love him intensely, a love that was natural, not a legal one. When death approached him and his time came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him to faith and to enter Islam. So fate overtook him and snatched him from his hand, so he continued in his disbelief. And to God belongs perfect wisdom. Az-Zuhri said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me on the authority of his father, who is Al-Musayyab bin Hazn Al-Makhzumi may God be pleased with him, who said: When the death of Abu Talib was approaching, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to him and found Abu Jahl bin Hisham and Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah bin Al-Mughira with him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O uncle, say ‘There is no god but God,’ a word with which I will argue for you before God. Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah said: O Abu Talib, do you desire to abandon the religion of Abdul Muttalib? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept presenting it to him and they kept repeating that statement to him until the last thing he said was: He is on the religion of Abdul Muttalib, and he refused to say: There is no god but God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, I will seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so. Then God, the Most High, revealed: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives. And He revealed about Abu Talib: Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. They both included it from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, and Muslim narrated it in this way, and Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Yazid bin Kaysan from Abu Hazim from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the death of Abu Talib was approaching, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and said: “O my uncle, say: There is no god but God, and I will bear witness to it for you on the Day of Resurrection.” He said: “Were it not that the Quraysh would reproach me with it, saying: ‘What made him do it was only the fear of death,’ I would have made you happy with it. I do not say it except to make you happy with it.” Then God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. “He wills, and He knows best who are the guided.” Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib, we do not know it except from the hadith of Yazid ibn Kaysan. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan on the authority of Yazid ibn Kaysan: Abu Hazim told me on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and he mentioned it in a similar manner. Ibn Abbas, Ibn `Umar, Mujahid, al-Sha`bi, and Qatadah said the same: It was revealed about Abu Talib when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, offered him to say, There is no god but God, but he refused and said, O nephew, follow the religion of the elders. The last thing he said was, I follow the religion of `Abd al-Muttalib. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Salamah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khaitham told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, who said: “Caesar’s messenger came to me and said: Caesar wrote a letter to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with me. So I went to him and gave him the letter, and he put it in his lap. Then he said: ‘From whom is this man?’ I said: ‘From Tanukh.’ He said: ‘Do you want to follow the religion of your father Ibrahim, the Hanifite?’ I said: ‘I am the messenger of a people and I will follow their religion until I return to them.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed and looked at his companions and said: ‘You do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills.’” God the Almighty says: And they say, ‘If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.’ God the Almighty is informing us about the excuse of some of the disbelievers for not following the guidance, when they said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land. That is, we fear that if we follow the guidance you have brought and oppose the polytheistic Arab tribes around us, they will intend to harm and fight us, and snatch us away wherever we are. God the Almighty said, answering them: Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary? This means that this excuse they made is a lie and a falsehood, because God the Almighty made them in a secure country and a respected sanctuary that has been secure since it was established. So how can this sanctuary be secure for them while they are disbelievers and polytheists, and not be secure for them when they have submitted and followed the truth? And the Almighty’s saying: The fruits of all things are brought to it meaning from all the fruits around it from Taif and other places, as well as the merchandise and goods as provision from Us meaning from Us but most of them do not know. That is why they said what they said. Al-Nasa’i said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad informed us, Al-Hajjaj informed us from Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abi Malekah informed me, he said: Amr bin Shuaib said from Ibn Abbas, and he did not hear it from him, that Al-Harith bin Amir bin Nawfal who said, If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.

28:58: God, the Almighty, is denouncing the people of Mecca in His statement: And how many a city have We destroyed which was insolent in its life meaning it became arrogant, rebellious, and disbelieved in the blessings of God in the provisions He bestowed upon them, as He says in the other verse: “And God presents an example: a city which was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location, but it denied the favors of God. So God made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing. And there had already come to them a messenger from themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.” For this reason, God, the Almighty, says: Those were their dwellings; they were not inhabited after them except for a little, meaning their homes were destroyed, so nothing could be seen except their dwellings. And God, the Almighty, says: And We were the inheritors, meaning it became ruined, with no one in it. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he heard Kaab say to Omar: “Solomon, peace be upon him, said to the owl - meaning the owl - ‘Why don’t you eat the crops?’ It said: ‘Because Adam was expelled from Paradise because of him.’ He said: ‘Why don’t you drink water?’ It said: ‘Because God drowned the people of Noah because of it.’ He said: ‘Why do you only go to ruins?’” She said, Because it is the inheritance of God Almighty. Then he recited, And We are the inheritors. Then God Almighty said, informing about His justice and that He does not destroy anyone who is unjust to Him, but rather He destroys from your people after the proof has been established against them. For this reason, He said, And your Lord would not destroy the cities until He had sent to their mother, which is Mecca, a messenger reciting to them Our verses. This indicates that the unlettered Prophet, namely Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, who was sent from the mother of cities, was a messenger to all the cities, Arabs and non-Arabs, as God Almighty said, To warn the mother of cities and those around it. And God Almighty said, “Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all. ’” And He said, To warn you with it and whomever it reaches. And He said, And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties, the Fire is his promised destination. The completion of the proof is God Almighty’s saying, And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. So God Almighty informed that He will destroy every city before the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty said, And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. So God Almighty made the mission of the unlettered Prophet inclusive of all the cities. Because he is a messenger to her mother and her origin to whom she returns. It is proven in the two Sahihs that he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: I was sent to the red and the black. For this reason, the prophethood and message were sealed with him, so there is no prophet or messenger after him, rather his law remains as long as night and day remain until the Day of Resurrection. It was said that what is meant by his saying: until He sends a messenger to her mother is her origin and her greatness like the mothers of villages and regions. This was narrated by Al-Zamakhshari, Ibn Al-Jawzi and others, and it is not far-fetched.

28:60: God Almighty says, informing us of the insignificance of this world, and the lowly adornments and fleeting splendors in it, in comparison to what God has prepared for His righteous servants in the Hereafter of great and lasting bliss, as God Almighty says: Whatever you have will perish, but what is with God is everlasting. And He says: And what is with God is better for the righteous. And He says: And what is the life of this world compared to the Hereafter is nothing but enjoyment. And He says: But you prefer the life of this world, * While the Hereafter is better and more lasting. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, what is the life of this world compared to the Hereafter except as one of you dips his finger in the sea, so let him see what he brings back. God the Almighty says: {Then will you not reason?} meaning, will he not reason who prefers this world over the Hereafter? It has also been said about Hamzah, Ali and Abu Jahl, both of them from Mujahid. It appears that it is general. This is like God the Almighty’s statement, informing about that believer when he looked down upon his companion while he was in the ranks, and that one was in the lowest levels, so He said: {And had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth.} God the Almighty says: {And Paradise has certainly known that they will be brought forth.}

This is by way of rebuke and threat, as God the Almighty says: “And you have certainly come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We gave you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners among you. The relationship between you has been severed, and lost from you is what you used to claim.” And His statement: Those against whom the word has come true will say, meaning the devils, the rebellious ones, and those who call to disbelief, “Our Lord, these are the ones we misled. We misled them as we were misled. We disavow ourselves to You. They used to worship us.” So they testified against them that they misled them, so they followed them, then disavowed their worship, as God Almighty said: “And they have taken other than God gods that they might be a source of honor for them. No! They will disbelieve in their worship and will be opponents to them.” And God Almighty said: “And who is more astray than he who invokes other than God those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their invocation, are unaware. And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship.” And Abraham, peace be upon him, said to his al-Nas 114:“You have only taken idols other than God out of affection among yourselves in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will disbelieve in one another and curse one another.” And God Almighty said: “When those who followed disown those who followed and they see the punishment and all ties are severed from them. Mujahid said: So the arguments will be blind to them, so they will not ask about lineages. 28:68: God Almighty informs us that He is the One who is unique in creation and choice, and that He has no rival or challenger in that. God Almighty says: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses meaning whatever He wills, so whatever He wills will be and whatever He does not will will not be, so all matters, good and bad, are in His hand and will be returned to Him. His statement: They have no choice is a negation according to the more correct of the two opinions, like God Almighty’s statement: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their decision Ibn Jarir chose that what here means which meaning: and chooses what is best for them. The Mu’tazila group used this approach as evidence for the necessity of taking into account what is best, but the correct view is that it is a negation, as Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas and others as well. The point is to explain that God Almighty is unique in creation, estimation and choice, and that He has no equal in that. That is why He said, Glory be to God, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him, meaning idols and rivals who do not create or choose anything. Then God the Almighty said: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare. That is, He knows what the inner thoughts conceal and what the secrets conceal, just as He knows what the outward appearances of all creation reveal. Alike among you is he who conceals his speech and he who declares it, he who hides it and he who conceals it and he who travels by day. And His statement, And He is God, there is no deity except Him means He is the One alone in divinity, so there is no deity worthy of worship other than Him, just as there is no Lord who creates what He wills and chooses other than Him. To Him be praise in the first and the last meaning in everything He does. He is the One who is praised for His justice and wisdom. And His is the judgment meaning there is no one who can question His power, might, wisdom and mercy. And to Him you will be returned meaning all of you on the Day of Resurrection. He will reward every worker for his deeds, good and evil, and nothing of them will be hidden from Him in all of their deeds.

And His statement, And He is God, there is no deity except Him means He is the One alone in divinity, so there is no deity worthy of worship other than Him, just as there is no Lord who creates what He wills and chooses other than Him. To Him be praise in the first and the last meaning in everything He does. He is the One who is praised for His justice and wisdom. And His is the judgment meaning there is no one who can question His power, might, wisdom and mercy. And to Him you will be returned meaning all of you on the Day of Resurrection. He will reward every worker for his deeds, good and evil, and nothing of them will be hidden from Him in all of their deeds.
28:70: God Almighty informs us that He is the One who is unique in creation and choice, and that He has no rival or challenger in that. God Almighty says: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses meaning whatever He wills, so whatever He wills will be and whatever He does not will will not be, so all matters, good and bad, are in His hand and will be returned to Him. His statement: They have no choice is a negation according to the more correct of the two opinions, like God Almighty’s statement: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their decision Ibn Jarir chose that what here means which meaning: and chooses what is best for them. The Mu’tazila group used this approach as evidence for the necessity of taking into account what is best, but the correct view is that it is a negation, as Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn Abbas and others as well. The point is to explain that God Almighty is unique in creation, estimation and choice, and that He has no equal in that. That is why He said, Glory be to God, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him, meaning idols and rivals who do not create or choose anything. Then God the Almighty said: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare. That is, He knows what the inner thoughts conceal and what the secrets conceal, just as He knows what the outward appearances of all creation reveal. Alike among you is he who conceals his speech and he who declares it, he who hides it and he who conceals it and he who travels by day. And His statement, And He is God, there is no deity except Him means He is the One alone in divinity, so there is no deity worthy of worship other than Him, just as there is no Lord who creates what He wills and chooses other than Him. To Him be praise in the first and the last meaning in everything He does. He is the One who is praised for His justice and wisdom. And His is the judgment meaning there is no one who can question His power, might, wisdom and mercy. And to Him you will be returned meaning all of you on the Day of Resurrection. He will reward every worker for his deeds, good and evil, and nothing of them will be hidden from Him in all of their deeds.
28:71: The Almighty says, thanking His servants for the night and day He has subjected to them, without which they cannot exist. He explained that if He had made the night permanent and eternal for them until the Day of Resurrection, it would have harmed them, and their souls would have grown weary of it and become restricted by it. For this reason, the Almighty said: What god other than God could bring you light? That is, one by which you could see and be comforted by it? Do you not hear? Then the Almighty informed that if He had made the day permanent, that is, permanent and continuous until the Day of Resurrection, it would have harmed them, and their bodies would have grown tired and worn out from many movements and occupations. For this reason, the Almighty said: What god other than God could bring you a night in which you may rest? That is, one by which you may rest from your movements and occupations. Do you not see? * And of His mercy,” that is, to you, He has made for you the night and the day, that is, He created this and that, that you may rest therein, that is, in the night, and that you may seek of His bounty, that is, in the day by traveling and moving, and by movements and occupations. This is from the category of twisting and spreading. His statement: And perhaps you will be grateful means that you will thank God through various forms of worship during the night and day. Whoever misses something at night can make up for it during the day, or during the day can make up for it during the night, as God Almighty said: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires to be grateful. There are many verses on this subject.

28:74: This is also a second call by way of rebuke and reprimand to those who worshipped another god with God. The Lord Almighty calls them out before all witnesses and says: Where are My partners whom you claimed? That is, in this world. And We have extracted from every nation a witness. Mujahid said: He means a messenger. Then We said, ‘Bring your proof.’ That is, of the truth of what you claimed, that God has partners. So they knew that the truth belongs to God. That is, there is no god other than Him. So they did not speak and were not confused by an answer. And what they used to invent was lost to them. That is, they went away and did not benefit them.

28:76: Al-A'mash narrated on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Qarun was from the people of Moses. He said: He was his cousin. This is what Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i, Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal, Simak bin Harb, Qatadah, Malik bin Dinar, Ibn Jurayj and others said, that he was the cousin of Moses, peace be upon him. Ibn Jurayj said: He is Qarun bin Yashar bin Qahath and Moses bin Imran bin Qahath. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar claimed that Qarun was the uncle of Moses bin Imran, peace be upon him. Ibn Jurayj said: Most scholars agree that he was his cousin, and God knows best. Qatada bin Di'amah said: We used to say that he was the cousin of Moses, and he was called Al-Munwar because of the beauty of his voice reciting the Torah, but the enemy of God was a hypocrite just as the Samaritan was, so transgression destroyed him because of his great wealth. Shahr bin Hawshab said: He added a handspan to the length of his clothes to show superiority over his people. And His statement: {And We gave him of the treasures} meaning wealth, {the keys of which would be a burden to a band of strong men} meaning that carrying them would be a heavy burden for groups of people because of their large number. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Khaithamah: The keys to Qarun’s treasures were made of hides, each key the size of a finger, each key to a separate treasury. When he mounted them, they would be carried on sixty white-footed, white-footed mules. Other than that was said, and God knows best. And His statement: {When his people said to him, “Do not rejoice. Indeed, God does not like the exultant”} meaning that the righteous people of his people admonished him regarding what he was in, and they said by way of advice and guidance: Do not rejoice in what you have, meaning do not be arrogant about the wealth you have, Indeed, God does not like the exultant. Ibn Abbas said: He means the exultant. Mujahid said: He means the arrogant and haughty who do not thank God for what He has given them. And His statement: And seek, through that which God has given you, the home of the Hereafter, and do not neglect your share of this world. That is, use what God has given you of this abundant wealth and immense blessings in obeying your Lord and drawing closer to Him through various acts of worship, through which you will attain reward in this world and the next. And do not neglect your share of this world. That is, what God has permitted in it of food, drink, clothing, housing, and marriage. For your Lord has a right over you, and your soul has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, and your visitors have a right over you, so give each one their due. And do good as God has been good to you. That is, do good to His creation, as He has been good to you. And seek not corruption in the land. That is, do not let your concern with what you are doing be to corrupt the land and harm God’s creation. Indeed, God does not like corrupters.

28:78: God the Almighty says, informing about Qarun’s response to his people when they advised him and guided him to good: He said, ‘It was only given to me because of knowledge I have.’ That is, I do not need what you say, for God the Almighty only gave me this money because He knew that I deserved it and because He loved me. So His interpretation is that I only gave it to him because of God’s knowledge that I am worthy of it. This is like His statement, the Almighty: So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, ‘It was only given to me because of knowledge.’ That is, because of God’s knowledge of me. And like His statement, the Almighty: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after an adversity has touched him, he will surely say, ‘This is for me.’ That is, this is what I deserve. It was narrated that some of them meant, It was only given to me because of knowledge I have, meaning that he was studying chemistry. This statement is weak, because chemistry itself is a false science, because no one has power over the creation of things except God, the Almighty. God the Almighty said, “O mankind, an example is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides God will never create a fly, even if they banded together for that purpose.” In the Sahih, it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, God the Almighty says, ‘And who is more unjust than he who tries to create the like of My creation? So let them create an atom, let them create a barley grain.’ This was mentioned regarding the image-makers who resemble God’s creation in merely the outward image or form, so how about someone who claims that he transforms the essence of this entity into the essence of another entity? This is false and impossible, ignorance and misguidance. They are only able to paint in apparent images, which are lies, deception, camouflage and promoting that it is true in reality, but it is definitely not so, and it has not been proven by a legitimate way that it was true with anyone from this method that these ignorant, immoral and slanderous people practice. As for what God, the Most High, does of violating customs at the hands of some saints by turning some notables into gold or silver or the like, this is something that no Muslim denies, and no believer rejects. However, this is not from the category of industries, rather this is from the will of the Lord of the earth and heavens, His choice and His action, as it was narrated from Haywah ibn Shuraih al-Misri, may God have mercy on him, that a questioner asked him, and he did not have anything to give him, and he saw his need, so he took a pebble from the earth and rolled it in his hand, then threw it to the questioner, and it turned red gold. The hadiths and narrations on this are very many and it would take too long to mention. Some of them said: Qarun knew the Greatest Name, so he called upon God by it and became wealthy because of it. The first meaning is correct, and for this reason God Almighty said in response to his claim that God took care of him and gave him wealth: Did he not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were mightier than him in strength and greater in accumulation? That is, there were those who had wealthier than him, but that was not because they loved to attain it. God destroyed them because of their disbelief and lack of gratitude. For this reason He said: And the criminals will not be asked about their sins, meaning because of the abundance of their sins. Qatadah said: With knowledge I have means With goodness I have. Al-Suddi said: With knowledge that I am worthy of that. Imam Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam excelled in interpreting this verse, for he said regarding His statement, He said, ‘It was only given to me because of knowledge I have,’ that he said: If it were not for God’s pleasure with me and His knowledge of my virtue, He would not have given me this money. He then recited, Does he not know that God destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him in strength and greater in accumulation? The verse. And thus says one whose knowledge is little when he sees someone to whom God has given abundantly, were it not for his deserving of that, he would not have been given it.
28:79: God the Almighty says, informing us about Qarun that he came out one day to his people in great finery and dazzling beauty, with mounts and clothes for him and his servants and attendants. When those who desired the life of this world and were inclined towards its decorations and adornments saw him, they wished that they had what he was given, “Oh, would that we had like what Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.” That is, one of abundant fortune in this world. When the people of beneficial knowledge heard their words, they said to them, Woe to you! The reward of God is better for those who believe and do righteousness. That is, God’s reward for His believing, righteous servants in the Hereafter is better than what you see. As in the authentic hadith, “God the Most High says, ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.’ And read, if you wish, ‘No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do.’ And His statement, ‘And none shall attain it except the patient.’” Al-Suddi said, And none shall attain Paradise except the patient. It is as if He made that part of the statement of those who were given knowledge. Ibn Jarir said, And none shall attain this statement except those who are patient, refraining from the love of this world and desiring the Hereafter. It is as if He made that cut off from the statement of those, and made it part of the statement of God the Almighty and His information about that.

28:81: When God mentioned Qarun's ostentation in his finery and his pride before his people and his aggression against them, He then caused the earth to swallow him and his home, as was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari from the hadith of Az-Zuhri from Salim that his father told him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: While a man was dragging his garment, the earth swallowed him up, and he will continue to sink into the earth until the Day of Resurrection. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Jarir ibn Zayd from Salim from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said: An-Nadr ibn Ismail Abu Al-Mughira Al-Qass told us, Al-A’mash told us from Atiyyah from Abu Sa’id who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “While a man among those who came before you went out wearing two green cloaks, strutting about in them, God commanded the earth to swallow him, and he will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection.” Ahmad alone transmitted it, and its chain of transmission is good. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Abu Khaithama told us, Abu Ya’la bin Mansour told us, Muhammad bin Muslim told me, I heard Ziyad An-Namari narrating on the authority of Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “While a man among those who came before you went out wearing two cloaks and strutted about in them, God commanded the earth to take him, and he will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection.” Al-Hafiz Muhammad bin Al-Mundhir mentioned in his book Al-Aja’ib Al-Gharibah on the authority of Nawfal bin Masahiq who said: I saw a young man in the mosque of Najran, and I began to look at him and marvel at his height, perfection and beauty. He said: Why are you looking at me? I said: I marvel at your beauty and perfection. He said: God marvels at me. He said: So he kept getting smaller and smaller until he was the length of a handspan, and one of his relatives took him in his sleeve and went with him. It has been mentioned that the destruction of Qarun was due to the supplication of Moses, the Prophet of God, peace be upon him. There is a difference of opinion about its cause. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi that Qarun gave a prostitute money on the condition that she would slander Moses in the presence of the assembly of the Children of Israel while he was standing among them reciting to them the Book of God Almighty. She would say, O Moses, you did such and such to me. When she said that to Moses, peace be upon him, in the assembly, he trembled with fear and turned to her after praying two rak’ahs. Then he said, I ask you by God who parted the sea and saved you from Pharaoh, and did such and such, why did you tell me what made you say what you said? She said: As you asked me, Korah gave me such and such on the condition that I say that to you, and I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him. Then Moses fell down prostrating to God, the Almighty, and asked God about Korah, so God revealed to him that He has commanded the earth to obey you in it, so Moses commanded the earth to swallow him and his house, and that was it. It was said that when Korah came out to his people in that finery, riding on gray mules, and he and his servants were wearing purple dyed clothes, he passed in that gathering by the assembly of the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, and he was reminding them of the days of God, so when the people saw Korah, their faces turned towards him, looking at what he was doing, so Moses, peace be upon him, called him and said: What made you do what you did? He said: O Moses, if you have been given superiority over me in prophethood, then I have been given superiority over you in this world. If you wish, we will go out and you will supplicate against me and I will supplicate against you. So Moses went out and Korah went out with his people. Moses said: Will you supplicate or shall I supplicate? He said: Rather, I will supplicate. Korah supplicated but he was not answered. Then Moses said: Shall I supplicate? He said: Yes. Then Moses said: O God, command the earth to obey me today. Then God revealed to him that I have done so. Moses said: O earth, take them. So it took them to their feet. Then he said: Take them. So it took them to their knees, then to their shoulders. Then he said: Come with their treasures and wealth. He said: So it came with them until they saw it. Then Moses pointed with his hand and said: Go, sons of Levi. So the earth leveled them. And from Ibn Abbas, he said: They were swallowed up to the seventh earth. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that they will be swallowed up by the earth every day, and they will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection. Here, strange Israelite stories have been mentioned, which we have ignored. And the Almighty’s statement: But he had no company to aid him other than God, nor was he among those who defend themselves. That is, his wealth, his collection, his servants, and his retinue did not avail him, nor did they ward off from him the wrath, punishment, and chastisement of God, nor was he in himself a defender of himself, so he had no supporter from himself or from anyone else. And the Almighty’s saying: And those who wished to be in his place yesterday meaning those who, when they saw him in his finery, “Would that we had like that which Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.” So when the earth swallowed him up, they began to say, It is as if God expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it. That is, money is not an indication of God’s pleasure with its owner, for God gives and withholds, restricts and expands, lowers and raises, and He has perfect wisdom and a conclusive proof. This is as in the hadith attributed to Ibn Mas`ud: “God has divided your morals among you just as He has divided your provisions. God gives wealth to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He gives faith only to whomever He loves.” Had it not been for God’s favor upon us, He would have swallowed us up. That is, had it not been for God’s kindness and goodness to us, He would have swallowed us up just as He swallowed him up, because we wished to be like him. It is as if the disbelievers will not succeed. They mean that he was a disbeliever, and the disbelievers will not succeed with God, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. The grammarians differed over the meaning of His saying here, It is as if. He said: Some of them said: Its meaning is woe to you, know that, but it was shortened and it was said woe to you, and the opening of that indicated the deletion of know. Ibn Jarir weakened this saying, but it appears to be strong, and nothing is problematic about it except its writing in the copies of the Qur’an connected as wa-ka’anna, and writing is a conventional, conventional matter, and the reference is to the Arabic word, and God knows best. It was said that its meaning is wa-ka’anna, meaning did you not see that? Qatada said this. It was said that its meaning is wa-ka’anna, so he separated it and made the wa- for amazement or for alerting, and ka’anna means I think and I think. Ibn Jarir said: The strongest saying in this is the saying of Qatada that it means did you not see that, and he cited as evidence the saying of the poet: She asked me for divorce when she saw me. She said, Why have you come to me with something strange? It is as if the one who has a good lineage is loved, while the one who is poor lives a life of hardship.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Abu Khaithama told us, Abu Ya’la bin Mansour told us, Muhammad bin Muslim told me, I heard Ziyad An-Namari narrating on the authority of Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “While a man among those who came before you went out wearing two cloaks and strutted about in them, God commanded the earth to take him, and he will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection.” Al-Hafiz Muhammad bin Al-Mundhir mentioned in his book Al-Aja’ib Al-Gharibah on the authority of Nawfal bin Masahiq who said: I saw a young man in the mosque of Najran, and I began to look at him and marvel at his height, perfection and beauty. He said: Why are you looking at me? I said: I marvel at your beauty and perfection. He said: God marvels at me. He said: So he kept getting smaller and smaller until he was the length of a handspan, and one of his relatives took him in his sleeve and went with him. It has been mentioned that the destruction of Qarun was due to the supplication of Moses, the Prophet of God, peace be upon him. There is a difference of opinion about its cause. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi that Qarun gave a prostitute money on the condition that she would slander Moses in the presence of the assembly of the Children of Israel while he was standing among them reciting to them the Book of God Almighty. She would say, O Moses, you did such and such to me. When she said that to Moses, peace be upon him, in the assembly, he trembled with fear and turned to her after praying two rak’ahs. Then he said, I ask you by God who parted the sea and saved you from Pharaoh, and did such and such, why did you tell me what made you say what you said? She said: As you asked me, Korah gave me such and such on the condition that I say that to you, and I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him. Then Moses fell down prostrating to God, the Almighty, and asked God about Korah, so God revealed to him that He has commanded the earth to obey you in it, so Moses commanded the earth to swallow him and his house, and that was it. It was said that when Korah came out to his people in that finery, riding on gray mules, and he and his servants were wearing purple dyed clothes, he passed in that gathering by the assembly of the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, and he was reminding them of the days of God, so when the people saw Korah, their faces turned towards him, looking at what he was doing, so Moses, peace be upon him, called him and said: What made you do what you did? He said: O Moses, if you have been given superiority over me in prophethood, then I have been given superiority over you in this world. If you wish, we will go out and you will supplicate against me and I will supplicate against you. So Moses went out and Korah went out with his people. Moses said: Will you supplicate or shall I supplicate? He said: Rather, I will supplicate. Korah supplicated but he was not answered. Then Moses said: Shall I supplicate? He said: Yes. Then Moses said: O God, command the earth to obey me today. Then God revealed to him that I have done so. Moses said: O earth, take them. So it took them to their feet. Then he said: Take them. So it took them to their knees, then to their shoulders. Then he said: Come with their treasures and wealth. He said: So it came with them until they saw it. Then Moses pointed with his hand and said: Go, sons of Levi. So the earth leveled them. And from Ibn Abbas, he said: They were swallowed up to the seventh earth. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that they will be swallowed up by the earth every day, and they will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection. Here, strange Israelite stories have been mentioned, which we have ignored. And the Almighty’s statement: But he had no company to aid him other than God, nor was he among those who defend themselves. That is, his wealth, his collection, his servants, and his retinue did not avail him, nor did they ward off from him the wrath, punishment, and chastisement of God, nor was he in himself a defender of himself, so he had no supporter from himself or from anyone else. And the Almighty’s saying: And those who wished to be in his place yesterday meaning those who, when they saw him in his finery, “Would that we had like that which Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.” So when the earth swallowed him up, they began to say, It is as if God expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it. That is, money is not an indication of God’s pleasure with its owner, for God gives and withholds, restricts and expands, lowers and raises, and He has perfect wisdom and a conclusive proof. This is as in the hadith attributed to Ibn Mas`ud: “God has divided your morals among you just as He has divided your provisions. God gives wealth to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He gives faith only to whomever He loves.” Had it not been for God’s favor upon us, He would have swallowed us up. That is, had it not been for God’s kindness and goodness to us, He would have swallowed us up just as He swallowed him up, because we wished to be like him. It is as if the disbelievers will not succeed. They mean that he was a disbeliever, and the disbelievers will not succeed with God, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. The grammarians differed over the meaning of His saying here, It is as if. He said: Some of them said: Its meaning is woe to you, know that, but it was shortened and it was said woe to you, and the opening of that indicated the deletion of know. Ibn Jarir weakened this saying, but it appears to be strong, and nothing is problematic about it except its writing in the copies of the Qur’an connected as wa-ka’anna, and writing is a conventional, conventional matter, and the reference is to the Arabic word, and God knows best. It was said that its meaning is wa-ka’anna, meaning did you not see that? Qatada said this. It was said that its meaning is wa-ka’anna, so he separated it and made the wa- for amazement or for alerting, and ka’anna means I think and I think. Ibn Jarir said: The strongest saying in this is the saying of Qatada that it means did you not see that, and he cited as evidence the saying of the poet: She asked me for divorce when she saw me. She said, Why have you come to me with something strange? It is as if the one who has a good lineage is loved, while the one who is poor lives a life of hardship.
28:84: God the Almighty informs us that the Hereafter and its everlasting bliss that does not change or disappear, He made it for His believing and humble servants who do not desire exaltation on earth, meaning to be haughty and arrogant towards God's creation, or to cause corruption among them, as Ikrimah said: Exaltation means tyranny. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: Exaltation means transgression. Sufyan ibn Saeed al-Thawri said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin: Exaltation on earth means unjust arrogance, and corruption is taking money unjustly. Ibn Jurayj said: They do not desire exaltation on earth out of arrogance and haughtiness nor corruption by committing sins. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ash’ath al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Salam al-A’raj, on the authority of Ali, who said: A man may like the strap of his sandal to be better than the strap of his companion’s sandal, so it is included in the words of God the Almighty: “That is the home of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.” This is understood to mean if he intended thereby to boast and to be arrogant towards others, for that is reprehensible, as it is proven in the Sahih that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: It has been revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one boasts over another and no one transgresses against another. But if he likes that merely for the sake of adornment, then there is nothing wrong with it, as it is proven that a man said: O Messenger of God, I like my cloak and shoes to be nice, so is that arrogance? He said: No, God is beautiful and loves beauty. And God the Almighty said: Whoever brings a good deed meaning on the Day of Resurrection will have better than it meaning God’s reward is better than the servant’s good deed, so how can God multiply it many times over? This is the status of grace. Then He said: And whoever brings an evil deed - those who do evil will not be recompensed except for what they used to do as He said in the other verse: “And whoever brings an evil deed - their faces will be thrown into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?” This is the status of grace and justice.
28:85: God Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, to convey the message and recite the Qur’an to the people, and informing him that He will return him to a place of return, which is the Day of Resurrection, and He will ask him about the burdens of prophethood that He entrusted to him. For this reason, God Almighty said: He who enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely return you to a place of return, meaning He enjoined upon you to deliver it to the people. Will surely return you to a place of return, meaning to the Day of Resurrection, and He will ask you about that, as God Almighty said: Then We will surely question those to whom it was sent, and We will surely question the messengers. And God Almighty said: The Day God will assemble the messengers and say, ‘What was your response?’ And He said: And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, He who enjoined the Qur’an upon you will surely bring you back to a place of return. He means, He will bring you back to Paradise and then ask you about the Qur’an. Al-Suddi said it, and Abu Say’d said something similar. Al-Hakam ibn Abaan said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, He will surely bring you back to a place of return, meaning, to the Day of Resurrection. Malik narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He will surely bring you back to a place of return, to death. This is why there are chains of narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both. In some narrations, it says, He will bring you back to life on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said, He will bring you back to life on the Day of Resurrection. This was also narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Abu Qaz’ah, Abu Malik, and Abu Salih. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, “Yes, by God, he has a place of return. God will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection and then admit him to Paradise.” Other narrations have been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Bukhari said in the interpretation of his Sahih: Muhammad ibn Muqatil told us, Ya’la told us, Sufyan al-Asfari told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He will surely return you to a place of return, he said: to Mecca. This is how it was narrated by al-Nasa’i in the interpretation of his Sunan, and by Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Ya’la, who is Ibn Ubayd al-Tanafisi, and this is how it was narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, He will surely return you to a place of return, meaning He will surely return you to Mecca as He expelled you from it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, He will surely return you to a place of return, to your birthplace in Mecca. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar to this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Yahya ibn al-Juraaz, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Atiyyah, and al-Dahhak. And my father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us: Sufyan said: We heard it from Muqatil seventy years ago, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left Mecca and reached Al-Juhfah, he longed for Mecca, so God revealed to him: Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely bring you back to a place of return, to Mecca. This is from the words of Ad-Dahhak, which indicates that this verse was revealed in Medina, even though the entire Surah was revealed in Mecca. And God knows best. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding the words of God: will surely bring you back to a place of return, he said: This is one of the things that Ibn Abbas kept secret. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Na’im al-Qari’ that he said regarding His statement: He will return you to a place of return, he said: To Jerusalem. And this - and God knows best - goes back to the statement of those who interpreted it as the Day of Resurrection, because Jerusalem is the land of gathering and resurrection, and God is the Grantor of success in what is correct. The way to reconcile these statements is that Ibn Abbas interpreted it at one time as his return to Mecca, which is the conquest which, according to Ibn Abbas, is a sign of the approaching death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas also interpreted Surah When the help of God and the conquest come to the end of the Surah, as the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which was announced to him, and that was in the presence of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Umar agreed with him on that and said: I do not know of it other than what you know. For this reason, Ibn Abbas interpreted at another time his saying: He will return you to a place of return as death, and at another time as the Day of Resurrection which is after death, and at another time as Paradise which is his reward and destiny for carrying out God’s message and conveying it to the two kinds of beings: mankind and jinn, and because he is the most perfect of God’s creation, the most eloquent of God’s creation, and the most noble of God’s creation in general. And the Almighty said: “Say: My Lord knows best who has brought guidance and who is in clear error.” That is, say to those of your people who opposed you and denied you, O Muhammad, from among the polytheists and those who followed them in their disbelief: Say: My Lord knows best who is guided among you and me. And you will come to know for whom the final outcome will be in the Hereafter, and for whom the final outcome and victory will be in this world and the hereafter. Then the Almighty said, reminding His Prophet of His great blessing upon him and upon the servants when He sent him to them: And you did not expect that the Scripture would be revealed to you, meaning you did not think before the revelation was sent down to you that the revelation would be sent down to you, but it is a mercy from your Lord, meaning that the revelation was sent down to you from God out of His mercy towards you and the servants because of you. So if He grants you this great blessing, then never be a supporter, meaning a helper, of the disbelievers, but separate from them, oppose them, and disagree with them. And let not them turn you away from the verses of God after they have been sent down to you, meaning do not be affected by their opposition to you and their turning people away from your path. Do not turn away from that and do not care about it, for God is the one who will support your word, support your religion, and make manifest what He sent you with over all other religions. For this reason He said: And invite to your Lord, meaning to the worship of your Lord alone, with no partner, and do not be of those who associate others with Him. And His statement: “And do not invoke with God another deity. There is no deity except Him.” That is, worship is not appropriate for anyone except Him, and divinity is not appropriate except for His greatness. And His statement: Everything will perish except His Face is informing us that He is the Everlasting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, to whom creation dies but He does not die, as God the Most High said: Everything on it will perish, but the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain. So He expressed the Face as referring to the Self. And similarly His statement here: Everything will perish except His Face means except Him. It has been proven in the Sahih on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The most truthful statement that the poet Labid said is: ‘Beware, everything other than God is false.’” Mujahid and Ath-Thawri said regarding His statement: Everything will perish except His Face meaning except that by which His Face is intended. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih as confirmed by it. Ibn Jarir said: Those who say that cite as evidence the words of the poet: I ask forgiveness of God for a sin that I cannot count. To Him belongs the face and the action. This statement does not contradict the first statement, as this is a statement that all actions are invalid except for those done for the sake of God Almighty, from righteous deeds that are in accordance with the Shariah. The implication of the first statement is that all beings are perishable and fleeting except for His Essence, the Most High and Most Holy, for He is the First and Last, who is before everything and after everything. Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya said in the Book of Reflection and Consideration: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Umar bin Saleem Al-Bahili told us, Abu Al-Walid told us: When Ibn Umar wanted to examine his heart, he would go to a ruined place, stand at its door and call out in a sad voice, saying, Where are my people? Then he would come back to himself and say, Everything will perish except His Face. His statement, To Him belongs the judgement means the kingdom and control, and there is no question of His judgement. And to Him you will be returned means on the Day of Resurrection, and He will reward you for your deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil. End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Qasas. All praise and thanks are due to God.

This is how it was narrated by al-Nasa’i in the interpretation of his Sunan, and by Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Ya’la, who is Ibn Ubayd al-Tanafisi, and this is how it was narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, He will surely return you to a place of return, meaning He will surely return you to Mecca as He expelled you from it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, He will surely return you to a place of return, to your birthplace in Mecca. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar to this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Yahya ibn al-Juraaz, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Atiyyah, and al-Dahhak. And my father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us: Sufyan said: We heard it from Muqatil seventy years ago, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left Mecca and reached Al-Juhfah, he longed for Mecca, so God revealed to him: Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely bring you back to a place of return, to Mecca. This is from the words of Ad-Dahhak, which indicates that this verse was revealed in Medina, even though the entire Surah was revealed in Mecca. And God knows best. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding the words of God: will surely bring you back to a place of return, he said: This is one of the things that Ibn Abbas kept secret. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Na’im al-Qari’ that he said regarding His statement: He will return you to a place of return, he said: To Jerusalem. And this - and God knows best - goes back to the statement of those who interpreted it as the Day of Resurrection, because Jerusalem is the land of gathering and resurrection, and God is the Grantor of success in what is correct. The way to reconcile these statements is that Ibn Abbas interpreted it at one time as his return to Mecca, which is the conquest which, according to Ibn Abbas, is a sign of the approaching death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas also interpreted Surah When the help of God and the conquest come to the end of the Surah, as the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which was announced to him, and that was in the presence of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Umar agreed with him on that and said: I do not know of it other than what you know. For this reason, Ibn Abbas interpreted at another time his saying: He will return you to a place of return as death, and at another time as the Day of Resurrection which is after death, and at another time as Paradise which is his reward and destiny for carrying out God’s message and conveying it to the two kinds of beings: mankind and jinn, and because he is the most perfect of God’s creation, the most eloquent of God’s creation, and the most noble of God’s creation in general. And the Almighty said: “Say: My Lord knows best who has brought guidance and who is in clear error.” That is, say to those of your people who opposed you and denied you, O Muhammad, from among the polytheists and those who followed them in their disbelief: Say: My Lord knows best who is guided among you and me. And you will come to know for whom the final outcome will be in the Hereafter, and for whom the final outcome and victory will be in this world and the hereafter. Then the Almighty said, reminding His Prophet of His great blessing upon him and upon the servants when He sent him to them: And you did not expect that the Scripture would be revealed to you, meaning you did not think before the revelation was sent down to you that the revelation would be sent down to you, but it is a mercy from your Lord, meaning that the revelation was sent down to you from God out of His mercy towards you and the servants because of you. So if He grants you this great blessing, then never be a supporter, meaning a helper, of the disbelievers, but separate from them, oppose them, and disagree with them. And let not them turn you away from the verses of God after they have been sent down to you, meaning do not be affected by their opposition to you and their turning people away from your path. Do not turn away from that and do not care about it, for God is the one who will support your word, support your religion, and make manifest what He sent you with over all other religions. For this reason He said: And invite to your Lord, meaning to the worship of your Lord alone, with no partner, and do not be of those who associate others with Him. And His statement: “And do not invoke with God another deity. There is no deity except Him.” That is, worship is not appropriate for anyone except Him, and divinity is not appropriate except for His greatness. And His statement: Everything will perish except His Face is informing us that He is the Everlasting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, to whom creation dies but He does not die, as God the Most High said: Everything on it will perish, but the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain. So He expressed the Face as referring to the Self. And similarly His statement here: Everything will perish except His Face means except Him. It has been proven in the Sahih on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The most truthful statement that the poet Labid said is: ‘Beware, everything other than God is false.’” Mujahid and Ath-Thawri said regarding His statement: Everything will perish except His Face meaning except that by which His Face is intended. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih as confirmed by it. Ibn Jarir said: Those who say that cite as evidence the words of the poet: I ask forgiveness of God for a sin that I cannot count. To Him belongs the face and the action. This statement does not contradict the first statement, as this is a statement that all actions are invalid except for those done for the sake of God Almighty, from righteous deeds that are in accordance with the Shariah. The implication of the first statement is that all beings are perishable and fleeting except for His Essence, the Most High and Most Holy, for He is the First and Last, who is before everything and after everything. Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya said in the Book of Reflection and Consideration: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Umar bin Saleem Al-Bahili told us, Abu Al-Walid told us: When Ibn Umar wanted to examine his heart, he would go to a ruined place, stand at its door and call out in a sad voice, saying, Where are my people? Then he would come back to himself and say, Everything will perish except His Face. His statement, To Him belongs the judgement means the kingdom and control, and there is no question of His judgement. And to Him you will be returned means on the Day of Resurrection, and He will reward you for your deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil. End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Qasas. All praise and thanks are due to God.
